ownerApprovalsNeeded.affected: No scored MACS operation item; possible future companion after question.topic.adrenal-men-endocrine.confirm-cortisol-autonomy.v2
competingActions: Adrenalectomy for a unilateral MACS adenoma
ownerApprovalsNeeded.evidenceBoundary: AAES 2022 recommendation 3.1 broadly favors adrenalectomy; ESE 2023 R3.8/4.1 conditions the discussion on comorbidities, persistent autonomy, patient factors and expert review. Do not average this into a universal surgery rule.
ownerApprovalsNeeded.questionForMelissa: For a future patient with confirmed unilateral MACS but mild controlled comorbidities, which exact patient-specific findings and preferences should establish an operative versus surveillance key? Until that profile is approved, keep this teaching point unkeyed.

ownerApprovalsNeeded.affected: No scored young-patient exception item; current PA cases deliberately age 51-60
ownerApprovalsNeeded.evidenceBoundary: AAES 2022 describes a broader young-patient deferral approach; the retained Endocrine Society 2025 claim excludes the narrow very-young exception. A universal exact age/biochemistry shortcut is not established by this packet.
ownerApprovalsNeeded.questionForMelissa: Should a future exception case require all strict current phenotype and imaging criteria, and when would you still choose AVS despite those criteria? Approve the exact comparison and verify current journal guidance before authoring a keyed exception.

ownerApprovalsNeeded.evidenceBoundary: Both can be reasonable in a technically suitable hereditary remaining-gland case; patient recurrence-versus-replacement priorities and intact removal determine the tradeoff. A third ablation foil is not a credible peer. Feasibility alone does not select a universal operation.
ownerApprovalsNeeded.questionForMelissa: For a future remaining-gland hereditary tumor, what exact observed anatomy, oncologic constraints and patient priorities should determine a fair single best comparison between cortical preservation and total removal?

integrationDependencies: Manager alone changes the ship manifest, shared concept/case registries and timing/order/source-link registries after independent review.
Preserve B2A11 exact question and complete passed context; do not insert it after cortisol-classification feedback without new sequence review.
Preserve all thirteen exact clinically approved question definitions; existing canonicalized headers are separate materializations, not newly approved presentations.
Only clinic settings are used; operative and inpatient decisions review outside-care plans and records. No ICU/ED capability or new service is required.

All testing choices, including distractors, need exact timing-registry admission. Existing placeholder profiles supply estimates only. Every serviceRequest/resultGate is null; no uninstalled test is claimed to execute.
Isolated thyroid/parathyroid surgery, pancreatic tumor extent, and generic germline-testing methods remain other topics. MEN1 organ-specific companions need manager coordination.

The active preview has twenty standalone cases. Do not admit archived mixed multipart cases; recomposition requires every scored exact version to pass independent review and an additional sequence cue check.

Three originally standalone PASS cases are whole-case exact. Four splits preserve PASS wording and original full contexts; manager and independent reviewer must accept new composition. The alpha split adds required neutral completion metadata only.

Do not interpret a parked replacement as authorization to retire its existing inventory predecessors. The original audit retirement proposals remain historical pending alternative coverage or explicit manager disposition.

steps: Recognize concordant repeated cortisol abnormalities without an exogenous exposure explanation.
Choose biochemical source classification before either incidental-image pathway.
checks.closestError: Order pituitary MRI because an earlier scan already showed a focus.
checks.decidingObservation: The two images compete, while no basal ACTH classification is supplied.
checks.counterfactual: With suppressed ACTH already established on valid repeat sampling, adrenal-directed imaging becomes the appropriate branch.
checks.deletionTest: Both cortisol modalities establish the stage; exposure review preserves the endogenous boundary; the two incidental images create genuine competing source anchors.
checks.cueAttack: Removed 'endogenous Cushing already established' and 'classify etiologic pathway' from the old lead-in. All choices are specific investigations and none is uniquely comprehensive.
checks.stageAndCategory: First etiologic investigation after concordant cortisol evidence.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate because both images can attract a resident who localizes before classifying.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone. The preserved B2A11 source-imaging PASS remains a separate case; this feedback must not be placed immediately before it without renewed context review.
checks.repairRecord: Changed raw evidence and real anatomical competitors, preserving the ACTH-classification concept. Removed a four-sibling cosmetic repeat pattern.

distractorChecks.temptation: Anchors on an existing pituitary image.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The small pituitary focus does not establish an ACTH source without biochemical classification.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An established ACTH-dependent pathway could warrant pituitary-directed investigation.

distractorChecks.temptation: Anchors on the incidental adrenal nodule.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The incidental adrenal nodule is not proof of autonomous cortisol secretion.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Suppressed ACTH on valid sampling would direct adrenal evaluation.

steps: Interpret the prepared values together with the prediuretic hypokalemia and resistant hypertension.
Apply the narrow no-suppression branch while retaining functional lateralization before choosing surgery.
checks.closestError: Order saline suppression for every positive aldosterone-renin screen.
checks.decidingObservation: Prepared immunoassay aldosterone 28 ng/dL and PRA 0.1 ng/mL/h with the overt clinical phenotype.
checks.counterfactual: If the prepared aldosterone result were intermediate rather than overt, the blanket bypass conclusion would no longer follow.
checks.deletionTest: Acquisition, assay, units, phenotype and operative intent all set the guideline branch. No calculated ARR is repeated as a decorative extra value.
checks.cueAttack: Removed the old exhibit's conclusion 'overt renin-independent excess'. Three actual pathways have comparable labels; no unique explanation is embedded in the key.
checks.stageAndCategory: Next endocrine testing pathway for a surgical candidate.
checks.difficulty: Predicted hard: confirmation and lateralization are distinct decisions even when one step can be bypassed.
checks.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback concerns validity only. New valid numbers change the branch; earlier negative results are not used as current evidence.
checks.repairRecord: Reused N1 concept meaning, replaced its cue-heavy phenotype summary with raw prepared observations and narrowed the task.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses a universal positive-screen confirmation rule.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It adds mandatory suppression where the represented overt branch does not require it.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Less overt biochemistry in a surgical candidate can justify a specialist suppression test.

distractorChecks.temptation: Converts a strong biochemical diagnosis into CT-only side selection.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Bypassing suppression here does not mean bypassing functional lateralization.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A narrowly selected very young patient may be considered for a different AVS pathway; this 51-year-old is outside that exception.

steps: Check bilateral sampling adequacy and normalize aldosterone to cortisol rather than comparing raw concentration or CT nodules.
Use the right-to-left corrected ratio of six and the patient's operative choice to select right adrenalectomy.
checks.closestError: Operate on the left CT nodule.
checks.decidingObservation: Both samples are selective and the corrected secretory ratio is sixfold higher on the right.
checks.counterfactual: Change right aldosterone to 200 and left aldosterone to 2400 ng/dL with cortisol unchanged: corrected ratios become right 1 and left 6, reversing the operative side.
checks.deletionTest: Every table cell contributes to selectivity or normalization. Cosyntropin and prior normal cortisol screening fix the interpretation assumptions. The CT side is the competing anchor.
checks.cueAttack: The table does not print ratios or a laterality interpretation. Options are comparable treatment choices. No raw 'high' label appears beside the correct gland.
checks.stageAndCategory: Aldosterone-directed treatment after completed functional localization.
checks.difficulty: Predicted hard: sampling adequacy, concentration correction and imaging-functional discordance all matter to one treatment decision.
checks.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback explains why AVS is needed, but gives neither calculation nor the current side. The new table must be interpreted independently.
checks.repairRecord: Constructed original values and a left/right conflict instead of another question asking merely to order AVS.

distractorChecks.temptation: Chooses the visible nodule instead of the functional result.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The image is on the left, but the corrected secretory ratio is much higher on the right.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A valid left-dominant corrected AVS ratio would support left adrenalectomy.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats discordance with CT as automatically bilateral disease.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Medical therapy remains an option, but a patient who chose surgery has a supported unilateral functional target here.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Bilateral nonlateralizing AVS or a decision against surgery would favor targeted medical treatment.

steps: Calculate right selectivity as 22/20 and recognize an inadequately selected sample.
Withhold side assignment and obtain a valid localization study instead of substituting CT or invalid ratios.
checks.closestError: Calculate a left/right ratio without validating the right sample.
checks.decidingObservation: Right-labeled cortisol 22 versus peripheral 20 after cosyntropin.
checks.counterfactual: With both selectivity ratios well above five and clear unilateral corrected secretion, the completed AVS could guide surgery without repetition.
checks.deletionTest: Cosyntropin, all cortisol values and the operative goal determine validity and next action. The right nodule creates the CT-rescue error; the aldosterone cells show why raw values cannot repair wrong-site sampling.
checks.cueAttack: No sample is called 'failed' or 'nonselective' before answering. The task does not name a missing repeat. Three localization policies refer to specific existing tests.
checks.stageAndCategory: Localization policy before surgery after a questionable acquisition.
checks.difficulty: Predicted hard because an apparently completed AVS can be less definitive than its header implies.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no prior calculation or interpretation is supplied.
checks.repairRecord: New acquisition-validity objective; no unsupported unilateral-sampling rescue cutoff is taught.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses a visible nodule to rescue an invalid invasive test.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A failed functional sample does not convert an older patient's nodule into a proven secretory source.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A narrowly selected very young-patient pathway may be considered separately; not this 60-year-old.

distractorChecks.temptation: Computes ratios before checking that both tubes came from the intended veins.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A ratio based on an unselected right sample cannot support standard bilateral lateralization.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Technically selective bilateral samples would permit standard ratio interpretation.

steps: Interpret the repeated metabolite elevations plus an adrenal mass as a functioning adrenal concern in the hereditary context.
Use the actual urgency of the competing neck conditions to prioritize adrenal surgery.
checks.closestError: Operate on the node-positive thyroid cancer first because it is malignant.
checks.decidingObservation: Reliable repeatedly elevated metabolites, with no neck or calcium emergency overriding the elective sequence.
checks.counterfactual: With reliable negative adrenal biochemistry and no functional adrenal concern, thyroid surgery would regain priority.
checks.deletionTest: Regional thyroid spread makes the oncologic competitor credible; airway and acute-calcium observations preserve the nonemergency boundary. The new hormone observations earn the change in sequence.
checks.cueAttack: Preparation is shared in the task, not a uniquely careful key. All choices are actual operations with comparable scope; no option says 'without addressing the adrenal tumor'.
checks.stageAndCategory: First operation among the planned endocrine procedures.
checks.difficulty: Predicted hard because real oncologic urgency competes with the endocrine sequence, without inventing an emergency.
checks.sequenceCheck: Earlier feedback names the endocrine tests but does not give operative order. Later raw results must be interpreted.
checks.repairRecord: Reused the N3 operative-order identity, retained its old versions and replaced context labels with current measured findings. No thyroid/parathyroid extent is scored.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes the malignant lesion automatically over a functional endocrine hazard.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Regional thyroid spread is important but does not outweigh the represented functioning adrenal perioperative risk without an airway emergency.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A reliable negative adrenal assessment would change the sequence; a true airway emergency would require a different individualized emergency pathway.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats recurrent stones and biochemical hyperparathyroidism before the functional adrenal concern.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Chronic mild PTH-dependent hypercalcemia is not the immediate operative priority in this record.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: After adrenal control, a separate organ-specific parathyroid indication can be addressed in the appropriate sequence.

steps: Interpret marked metanephrine elevation with hypertension and an adrenal mass as the relevant functional physiology.
Prioritize alpha-directed preparation rather than choosing an initial drug from the tachycardia or a mixed-label shortcut.
checks.closestError: Start labetalol because it has both receptor labels.
checks.decidingObservation: No alpha-directed preparation has occurred in a markedly hypertensive functional tumor.
checks.counterfactual: Once alpha blockade controls the vascular phenotype but significant tachycardia persists, a heart-rate-directed add-on becomes appropriate.
checks.deletionTest: Blood pressure and pulse make competing physiological goals visible; medication chronology defines the initial stage. Metabolites and mass establish the functional context.
checks.cueAttack: All labels are single named oral medications with no explanatory qualifiers. The lead-in does not name alpha or beta blockade. The drug mechanisms must be known.
checks.stageAndCategory: Initial oral preoperative medication.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: labetalol is a credible mixed-receptor trap, not an absurd distractor.
checks.sequenceCheck: First node. Feedback deliberately stops at vascular preparation and does not prescribe the subsequent tachycardia drug.
checks.repairRecord: Adds an applied named-drug variant without changing the twelve approved MEN2 question versions.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats the conspicuous pulse before the vascular physiology.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Starting beta blockade before alpha blockade can aggravate catecholamine-mediated vasoconstriction.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Persistent tachycardia after adequate alpha blockade can justify adding a beta blocker.

distractorChecks.temptation: Assumes a mixed alpha/beta label guarantees the required sequence.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Its substantial beta-blocking effect does not make it an appropriate substitute for initial adequate alpha preparation in this setting.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A different non-PPGL hypertension indication may use labetalol; not as the represented first preparation drug.

steps: Calculate the absolute and relative increase using compatible maximal-diameter measurements.
Apply both components to change the management plan for an indeterminate lesion.
checks.closestError: Continue unchanged follow-up because the lesion is still below an old size shortcut.
checks.decidingObservation: 30 to 38 mm over nine months using the same measurement method.
checks.counterfactual: 30 to 33 mm over the same interval is only 10% and 3 mm, so this significant-growth trigger does not apply.
checks.deletionTest: Both diameters, method and interval are necessary; initial indeterminate rather than unequivocally benign status fixes the rule's scope. No extra symptoms or unrelated labs are added.
checks.cueAttack: The stem does not label the growth 'significant' or print the rule. Three concrete management pathways; the key is not the only action with a named clinical purpose.
checks.stageAndCategory: Management after completed interval imaging.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: both growth components and the lesion's original evidence status matter.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no prior explanation states the threshold.
checks.repairRecord: A new clinically applied growth decision, not a statistics methods exercise or a rule that growth proves malignancy.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses the absence of symptoms or distant disease as reassurance against significant local growth.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The new change crosses both growth components, so unchanged routine follow-up is not the best response.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Subthreshold growth without other concerning findings could support further interval imaging.

distractorChecks.temptation: Attempts to settle benign-versus-ACC behavior with a standard needle pathway.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Significant growth in this primary indeterminate lesion prompts surgical reassessment, not routine biopsy as a malignancy discriminator.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A management-changing suspected adrenal metastasis can have a different biopsy indication after hormonal exclusion.

steps: Reconstruct specimen versus drug administration order and reject the mislabeled post-dose result.
Choose the incidentaloma-appropriate suppression assessment rather than substitute an overt-Cushing assay.
checks.closestError: Use a normal urine or salivary result to clear mild adrenal autonomy after the mislabeled study.
checks.decidingObservation: The cortisol specimen was collected before the only recorded dexamethasone dose.
checks.counterfactual: If the record instead showed valid post-dose sampling with adequate suppression, none of these repeat screens would be required solely to repair acquisition.
checks.deletionTest: The two timestamps and absence of a later specimen establish the actual error. Incidental discovery without an overt phenotype fixes the appropriate testing pathway. Size is omitted because it did not earn the cortisol decision.
checks.cueAttack: All three choices are named cortisol assessments with similar scope. No choice is uniquely a cautious repeat versus an operation. The report title conflicts with raw chronology; both must be interpreted.
checks.stageAndCategory: Next cortisol investigation after auditing a prior specimen record.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate: the learner must reject the report label and distinguish mild-autonomy assessment from familiar overt-Cushing screens; no claim of high difficulty.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; the later imaging answer and its feedback are absent.
checks.repairRecord: One review-directed revision. Scored meaning changes from initial assay recall to acquisition validity plus assay selection, so a new concept version preserves the original screen history.

distractorChecks.temptation: Switches to another familiar cortisol screen after seeing a mislabeled result.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: These are useful in overt cortisol-excess evaluation but can be normal in mild adrenal autonomy and do not replace the indicated valid incidentaloma DST.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An overt Cushing evaluation can appropriately use repeated late-night saliva rather than this isolated incidentaloma pathway.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses a standard overt-Cushing test as interchangeable with an incidentaloma screen.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Normal urine cortisol would not reliably exclude mild adrenal autonomy; the initial indicated suppression assessment was never obtained.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Repeated urine free cortisol can be appropriate when evaluating overt cortisol excess in a different clinical presentation.

steps: Verify that the 6-HU value comes from a true unenhanced homogeneous lesion.
Apply that benign category despite a diameter exceeding the older size shortcut.
checks.closestError: Schedule annual imaging solely because the lesion is over four centimeters.
checks.decidingObservation: Homogeneous 4.2-cm lesion with true unenhanced attenuation of 6 HU.
checks.counterfactual: Changing the unenhanced value to an indeterminate 28 HU removes the no-further-imaging key; if observation is selected after assessment, interval CT is supported.
checks.deletionTest: Size creates the credible surveillance error; homogeneity and acquisition establish the deciding category. The post-DST result is shared completed endocrine context, not an update claimed to change the imaging answer.
checks.cueAttack: A concrete interval-surveillance foil replaces a second characterization-only foil. All choices are imaging follow-up plans; no interpretation sentence labels the mass benign before answering.
checks.stageAndCategory: Imaging follow-up after completed characterization.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate, matching the review's valid imaging reasoning rather than claiming another inference from normal cortisol.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone imaging decision with no prior cortisol question or redundant normal-result update.
checks.repairRecord: One revision fixes the exact post-DST limit terminology and adds the plausible size-driven surveillance alternative. Stable concept meaning retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Retains surveillance because the diameter exceeds four centimeters.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Interval imaging is supported for observed indeterminate lesions, not this unequivocally homogeneous 6-HU lesion.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An observed indeterminate lesion could appropriately have repeat CT or MRI within 6-12 months.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats every mass over four centimeters as requiring another characterization study.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Washout characterization is unnecessary once true unenhanced homogeneous low attenuation has already characterized the lesion.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A lesion not adequately characterized on true unenhanced imaging may warrant additional expert-selected characterization.

steps: Interpret vomiting plus the paired low dexamethasone concentration as inadequate suppression-test exposure.
Choose a validity-repaired confirmation plan and basal ACTH classification rather than a specialized ACTH-dependent test.
checks.closestError: Obtain basal ACTH but retain the inadequate-exposure DST as proof of autonomy.
checks.decidingObservation: Paired serum dexamethasone was below the laboratory's validated exposure range after post-dose vomiting.
checks.counterfactual: With valid exposure on repeated nonsuppressing DST and ACTH independence already established, repeating this confirmation bundle would no longer be the next step.
checks.deletionTest: The measured exposure and vomiting establish actual interference. Normal urine/saliva create a credible reassurance error without replacing the mild-autonomy test. No sentence lists missing tests.
checks.cueAttack: A balanced 2-by-2 set repeats each confirmation and source component twice. The key is neither uniquely complete nor identifiable from a named absent ACTH result. Labels describe actions, with rationales kept after choice.
checks.stageAndCategory: Comparable confirmation plus source-assessment plans before a treatment decision.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: the nearest choice contains the right source assay but leaves the acquisition failure unresolved.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone with all actual collection observations visible before selection.
checks.repairRecord: One revision replaces missing-information cues with measured interference and explicitly tests how to repair it. Concept meaning remains confirmation with validity/ACTH assessment.

distractorChecks.temptation: Recognizes the failed exposure but jumps to pituitary-source testing.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: This repairs exposure but substitutes a specialized ACTH-dependent investigation for the initial basal ACTH classification.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Established ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism can create a later specialist role for CRH testing.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses the correct source assay while accepting a confounded cortisol result.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Basal ACTH is appropriate for classification, but it cannot turn this demonstrably low-exposure DST into valid confirmation.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: If the original DST had valid drug exposure, confirmed nonsuppression could be used with basal ACTH assessment.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats visible adrenal anatomy and an abnormal heading as enough to skip basic validity and source checks.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Both the confirmation and source-assessment stages are mishandled: inadequate exposure remains unresolved and ACTH dependence is not established.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Valid confirmed ACTH-dependent disease would change both prerequisites and could make specialist CRH testing relevant.

steps: Use suppressed ACTH to resolve competing pituitary and adrenal anatomical findings.
Apply the unilateral adrenal anatomy and overt-disease operative goal to choose left adrenalectomy.
checks.closestError: Remove the pituitary focus because an MRI lesion is mistaken for functional source proof.
checks.decidingObservation: ACTH is repeatedly below the assay reporting limit despite confirmed cortisol excess.
checks.counterfactual: With a confirmed pituitary ACTH source instead, the same pituitary focus would support a different operation; imaging alone would still be insufficient.
checks.deletionTest: The pituitary focus now earns ACTH interpretation. Overt symptoms and repeated studies distinguish the case from held MACS policy; side and contralateral anatomy select unilateral treatment.
checks.cueAttack: Two genuine anatomical targets prevent selecting by lesion-removal wording alone. The third bilateral operation represents over-treatment; no gland is called causal before selection.
checks.stageAndCategory: Definitive source operation after endocrine assessment.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate; the pituitary alternative is now credible, but this is not represented as a high-difficulty localization algorithm.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no earlier classification feedback or later replacement answer is visible.
checks.repairRecord: One revision introduces a competing pituitary finding while retaining essential adrenal anatomy. Stable overt-source operative concept retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses definitive bilateral cortisol-source removal despite a unilateral treatable source.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The record supports a unilateral source and does not justify removing the normal contralateral gland.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Selected bilateral adrenal disease or refractory ACTH-dependent disease can require a different operative strategy.

distractorChecks.temptation: Anchors on the pituitary MRI rather than the biochemical source pathway.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A pituitary focus is not proof of an ACTH source when ACTH is repeatedly suppressed.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An established pituitary ACTH source would make pituitary surgery appropriate.

steps: Infer temporary functional cortisol suppression despite preserved contralateral adrenal anatomy.
Select hydrocortisone for the affected pathway rather than mineralocorticoid replacement or omission.
checks.closestError: Omit replacement because the remaining adrenal looks normal.
checks.decidingObservation: The removed lesion produced overt cortisol excess with repeatedly suppressed preoperative ACTH; the postoperative axis has not recovered by documented testing.
checks.counterfactual: Documented axis recovery would change the need for continued hydrocortisone; primary mineralocorticoid deficiency would instead add a separate replacement need.
checks.deletionTest: The outside pre-discharge consultation fixes the time and site. Prior overt secretion and preserved right gland determine the endocrine inference; no future clinic visit is confused with current inpatient planning.
checks.cueAttack: Three specific replacement plans with comparable follow-up scope; neither the presentation nor task states a hormone deficiency or replacement need.
checks.stageAndCategory: Adrenal replacement plan before outside-hospital discharge.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate, retaining the review's supported two-step endocrine reasoning.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone postoperative record includes the necessary prior secretion and procedure; no operative-target feedback is required.
checks.repairRecord: One revision clarifies the pre-discharge chart-review frame, names medicines and explains preserved mineralocorticoid physiology. Stable concept retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats postoperative axis suppression as loss of all adrenal hormone function.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: This is ACTH-related cortisol suppression; aldosterone is generally preserved, and mineralocorticoid replacement does not address the expected cortisol deficit.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Documented primary aldosterone deficiency would create a role for fludrocortisone, alongside appropriate glucocorticoid care.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses an anatomical shortcut to omit needed replacement.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: An intact right adrenal gland does not prove immediate cortisol sufficiency after removal of an overt autonomous source.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Adequate documented postoperative cortisol reserve in a non-cortisol-secreting surgical case would change this plan.

steps: Use the pre-diuretic history and measured acquisition record to recognize a potentially false-negative screen.
Repair both potassium and the named interfering medication before repeating biochemistry.
checks.closestError: Correct potassium but repeat on unchanged chlorthalidone and accept the next negative result as exclusion.
checks.decidingObservation: Potassium was 2.8 mmol/L during aldosterone/renin sampling while taking chlorthalidone, and hypokalemia predated that prescription.
checks.counterfactual: A potassium-replete prepared negative screen without an interfering medication would remove these reasons for repetition; an unsafe withdrawal context would require a different supervised strategy.
checks.deletionTest: The pre-treatment potassium chronology prevents dismissing the phenotype as drug-induced. Sample conditions and medicine identity drive the repair. Blood pressure and creatinine describe current care, without a key-specific permission sentence.
checks.cueAttack: Four parallel preparation plans form a balanced potassium-by-medication matrix. Each component appears twice. No mechanistic drug label or clinician-availability endorsement supplies the answer.
checks.stageAndCategory: Preparation for the same repeat aldosterone-renin investigation.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate: a partially correct preparation plan is the nearest credible error; the matrix requires interpreting both actual confounders.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone before any later prepared positive result or suppression/localization feedback.
checks.repairRecord: One revision names chlorthalidone, supplies raw sampling data and compares actual corrective plans. Existing acquisition-repair concept retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Addresses the conspicuous low potassium while overlooking the actual medication.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Potassium correction repairs one problem, but the identified interfering diuretic remains a reason for a false-negative screen.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: When medication withdrawal is unsafe, a specialist may interpret on-treatment results or use a modified strategy; that restriction is not established here.

distractorChecks.temptation: Fixes medication interference but treats the potassium value as merely a symptom.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Changing the drug does not repair the low-potassium suppression of aldosterone at repeat sampling.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Once potassium is within range, additional potassium correction is not required simply to perform the screen.

distractorChecks.temptation: Assumes duplication of a result compensates for unchanged preparation errors.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Repeating the same confounded acquisition does not make the negative evaluation reliable.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Already suitable potassium and noninterfering medication conditions would not require these preparation changes.

steps: Verify bilateral selectivity, then correct each raw aldosterone value for cortisol rather than compare raw concentrations.
Choose targeted medical therapy for nonlateralizing secretion despite the CT nodule.
checks.closestError: Resect the left nodule because left raw aldosterone is twice the right value.
checks.decidingObservation: Both selective samples have the same aldosterone/cortisol ratio despite different raw concentrations.
checks.counterfactual: Changing left aldosterone to 14400 with cortisol still 400 gives a left/right corrected ratio of 6 and would change the treatment discussion toward a unilateral source.
checks.deletionTest: Raw paired values distinguish adequate bilateral sampling from both failed sampling and anatomical anchoring. Actual potassium/creatinine replace the MRA-permission sentence. Cortisol suppression supports the correction assumption.
checks.cueAttack: No precomputed SI/LI, bilateral label, experienced-center endorsement or drug-class permission appears before choice. Alternatives represent CT anchoring and invalid-study inference, rather than an unsupported right operation.
checks.stageAndCategory: PA treatment pathway after completed functional localization.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard because raw left concentration and CT agree while corrected secretion contradicts that impression.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no prior AVS feedback supplies the computation or treatment branch.
checks.repairRecord: One revision replaces interpreted ratios with conflicting raw data and actual safety observations. Stable bilateral-treatment concept retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses the larger raw concentration and visible nodule as convergent but misleading laterality evidence.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The left raw aldosterone is higher, but so is cortisol; corrected secretion is equal. The nodule does not establish a left functional source.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Valid left-lateralizing corrected secretion in an operative candidate would change the plan.

distractorChecks.temptation: Confuses symmetric corrected secretion with an uninterpretable study.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The cortisol gradients establish bilateral sampling adequacy; nonlateralization is not itself technical failure.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A nonselective side would prevent reliable lateralization and justify expert repeat sampling.

steps: Interpret the mild result using actual collection posture, stress and reference population.
Choose a valid basal metanephrine assessment before persistent-result suppression testing or an inferior analyte substitution.
checks.closestError: Order clonidine suppression as though the marginal normetanephrine elevation had already persisted under controlled conditions.
checks.decidingObservation: Only the stressed seated sample is abnormal; no comparable rested basal sample has yet been obtained.
checks.counterfactual: Repeated equivocal noradrenergic elevation under controlled collection would change the role of specialist suppression testing; a urine fractionated-metanephrine alternative would be valid rather than a foil.
checks.deletionTest: Collection and reference details must stay because validity is the inference. Cancer history, tissue impact and FDG uptake establish the consequence of prematurely clearing biopsy, rather than offering redundant imaging.
checks.cueAttack: All three options are specific endocrine biochemical investigations. The acquisition-repair key no longer competes against two unrelated imaging scans. Necessary collection words remain; no second accepted initial metanephrine assay is offered as a distractor.
checks.stageAndCategory: Next biochemical investigation before a pending adrenal tissue decision.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate ceiling: acquisition details necessarily point toward a repeat, but the closest endocrine suppression alternative now requires understanding the care phase. No hard label is asserted.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; the returned biopsy companion is parked, so no safety-feedback rehearsal is scored afterward.
checks.repairRecord: One revision preserves required acquisition facts and substitutes comparable endocrine plans with explicit analyte distinctions. Stable acquisition-review meaning retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Escalates directly to a familiar confirmatory test before establishing a valid baseline.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Clonidine is a specialized option for persistent equivocal noradrenergic findings; it does not repair the original mismatched basal collection.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Persistent equivocal normetanephrine elevation after controlled collection could support specialist clonidine testing.

distractorChecks.temptation: Switches to a urine test but chooses catecholamines rather than fractionated metanephrines.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Catecholamine measurements do not provide the preferred metanephrine-based assessment needed to resolve this prebiopsy question.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: If the laboratory request were urinary fractionated metanephrines, that would be an accepted initial biochemical alternative and could not fairly serve as this distractor.

steps: Recognize that the reported negative adrenal panel contains catecholamines rather than metanephrines.
Select the appropriate biochemical assessment still required before the planned thyroid operation.
checks.closestError: Repeat the same catecholamines during a spell instead of correcting the analyte selection.
checks.decidingObservation: The report's only analytes are plasma epinephrine and norepinephrine despite its 'adrenal screen normal' heading.
checks.counterfactual: If the prior record instead documented adequate recent plasma free metanephrines, repeating solely because of this wrong-analyte concern would not be justified.
checks.deletionTest: RET-associated MTC fixes the preoperative indication; the actual assay list supplies the validity obstacle. Normal calcium/PTH closes the earlier stone-related assessment rather than supplying an operation-order answer.
checks.cueAttack: All alternatives are biochemical tests with paired analytes and comparable scope. No component matrix is used after shifting from organ association to analyte adequacy; the task does not name the missing test.
checks.stageAndCategory: Next biochemical assessment before elective thyroid surgery.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate: the negative report heading and symptom-timed repeat are credible sources of error; no claim that recognizing RET alone supplies two steps.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; the exact PASS operation-priority node is separated with its original context.
checks.repairRecord: One revision materially changes organ-panel recall into prior-assay validity plus test selection. New concept version explicitly retains the prior MEN2 workup identity/history.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats sampling outside a spell as the only defect in the prior panel.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Intermittent catecholamine secretion and less accurate analytes make a symptom-timed repeat an inadequate substitute for the indicated screen.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A different catecholamine-physiology question can use these analytes; it would not establish completion of this MEN2 metanephrine assessment.

distractorChecks.temptation: Assumes a longer collection corrects the wrong-analyte limitation.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Changing the specimen to urine still selects catecholamines rather than fractionated metanephrines.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A request for urinary fractionated metanephrines would be an accepted alternative and would not be a fair distractor.

steps: Interpret the actual treated hemodynamic response and persistent symptomatic sinus tachycardia after reviewing competing causes.
Add rate control while maintaining established alpha protection rather than escalate or remove it.
checks.closestError: Replace doxazosin with metoprolol now that the pressure has fallen.
checks.decidingObservation: Repeated current pulse 124-126/min with limiting palpitations persists after alpha preparation, while current pressures are 116-118/72-74 without orthostatic symptoms.
checks.counterfactual: Ongoing hypertension before adequate alpha preparation would shift toward further alpha management; an identified volume or acute-illness cause would first require its correction.
checks.deletionTest: Actual repeat values replace low-normal and persistent labels. Symptoms establish clinical importance; sinus rhythm, hydration and concise competing-cause review bound the rate-control question. Initial vitals are omitted from this standalone treated-state case.
checks.cueAttack: Three parallel concrete changes to the same named medicines; no availability or treatment-permission statement appears in the pre-answer record.
checks.stageAndCategory: Medication adjustment during established preoperative adrenergic preparation.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate, retaining the valid two-step response-to-treatment objective with explicit tolerance/severity observations.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone treated-state record; the exact PASS initial-medication question is preserved separately.
checks.repairRecord: One revision supplies actual repeated vitals, symptom burden and concise alternative-cause observations without inventing universal thresholds. Stable meaning retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Continues escalating the initial medication despite a changed limiting problem.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The current pressure response and absence of ongoing hypertensive spells do not support escalating alpha blockade to treat the residual sinus rate.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Persistent hypertension from incomplete alpha preparation would make further alpha adjustment relevant.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats the medication sequence as a temporary prerequisite that can be discarded once pressure improves.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Replacing established alpha protection with beta blockade recreates the unsafe sequence while the catecholamine-producing tumor remains.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: After definitive tumor treatment and reassessment, the need for each agent can change; that is not this preoperative state.

steps: Interpret primary-adrenal morphology, endocrine results, staging and anatomical extent rather than assume adrenal metastasis or unresectable disease.
Select upfront resection sequencing without obligatory biopsy or systemic pretreatment when complete resection appears feasible.
checks.closestError: Require core histology before any resection plan despite the primary-adrenal resectable context.
checks.decidingObservation: No extra-adrenal primary or distant lesions, no great-vessel encasement/thrombus, and no extension beyond the stated kidney interface are seen.
checks.counterfactual: Great-vessel or multi-organ involvement precluding R0 removal would change the sequence toward expert biopsy/systemic or neoadjuvant assessment rather than the upfront key.
checks.deletionTest: Actual hormonal results replace a completed-workup label. Anatomical extent and staging now decide sequence; no generic expert-referral choice is offered. Possible kidney contact does not equal unresectability or mandate renal removal.
checks.cueAttack: Every choice is a concrete oncologic sequence at the same center, with planned resection or reassessment. The key has no unique cautious referral language. Expert review remains common background.
checks.stageAndCategory: Initial oncologic treatment sequence after endocrine and staging assessment.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: routine tissue-first care and treating large size as a systemic-therapy indication are credible competing errors.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no earlier feedback provides biopsy policy and no later invasion update is needed.
checks.repairRecord: One revision changes generic referral selection into resection-versus-biopsy/neoadjuvant sequence. New concept version preserves the prior generic pathway meaning and history; low-certainty sequencing evidence is recorded.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies a common histology-before-cancer-surgery habit to a setting where routine adrenal biopsy is not a prerequisite.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Routine biopsy does not improve the required sequence for an apparently resectable suspected primary cortical malignancy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Management-changing suspected metastasis or unresectable disease requiring systemic treatment can have a tissue-first pathway after endocrine exclusion.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats size or cancer suspicion as sufficient reason to delay potentially complete local treatment for systemic therapy.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: This is a systemic ACC pathway, but no distant disease or anatomy preventing initial complete resection is shown to justify making it mandatory before surgery here.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Initially unresectable disease in which complete removal is not feasible can justify expert consideration of neoadjuvant treatment; the exact regimen remains clinician-directed.

steps: Interpret the renal parenchymal extension and contour disruption as actual local invasion rather than simple contact.
Combine intact complete removal of involved tissue with the open approach appropriate to this invasive tumor.
checks.closestError: Use open exposure but peel the mass from an actually invaded kidney interface.
checks.decidingObservation: Enhancing tissue crosses from the adrenal mass into renal parenchyma and interrupts the renal contour.
checks.counterfactual: A preserved noninvaded plane would remove the requirement to resect kidney solely for contact; a smaller noninvasive lesion would also change the approach discussion.
checks.deletionTest: Raw invasion evidence replaces the expert prescription to remove organs together. Size, staging and patent vessels bound the local operative goal without a vague permission to undergo the proposed operation.
checks.cueAttack: Three specific operations; both foils preserve a credible part of the operative goal. No pre-answer phrase states combined removal, and deliberately incomplete debulking is removed.
checks.stageAndCategory: Operative approach and tissue-handling plan for a localized invasive adrenal mass.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: access and removal extent must both fit the anatomy; an open but separating operation remains a credible close error.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone original morphology plus dedicated observations; no preceding resection feedback is shown.
checks.repairRecord: One revision removes both expert feasibility/permission cues, supplies observed invasion and replaces debulking with component-level operative competitors. Stable meaning retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Keeps the right tissue-removal goal but discounts the invasive anatomy when choosing exposure and intact handling.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Although it preserves the en bloc goal, a minimally invasive approach is not the preferred plan for this large locally invasive suspected cortical malignancy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A suitable noninvasive localized lesion can have a minimally invasive complete-resection plan; that is not the represented renal invasion.

distractorChecks.temptation: Chooses the correct access while treating parenchymal invasion as a separable adhesion.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Open exposure does not make separating through invaded renal tissue an appropriate intact complete-resection plan.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Mere contact with a demonstrated noninvaded plane can justify preservation rather than automatic renal resection.

steps: Distinguish a new clinical endocrine pattern from unchanged benign imaging and an earlier valid evaluation.
Use the specific metabolic and skeletal change to choose cortisol reassessment among endocrine assays.
checks.closestError: Repeat aldosterone-renin testing because of the longstanding hypertension while ignoring which findings have actually changed.
checks.decidingObservation: Diabetes treatment needs have risen and a low-trauma vertebral fracture occurred after the prior evaluation, while blood pressure and potassium remain stable.
checks.counterfactual: If comorbidities and endocrine symptoms remained unchanged, routine repeat hormone testing would not be indicated; new hypokalemic resistant hypertension would instead change the prioritized axis.
checks.deletionTest: Chronology establishes a new reassessment trigger. Stable 7-HU morphology is the competing reassurance; actual stable pressure/potassium distinguish the nearest alternative axis. No prior washout acquisition is invented.
checks.cueAttack: All choices are named endocrine investigations with timing metadata. No CT/PET category foil remains, and neither the complaint nor presentation names a cortisol diagnosis.
checks.stageAndCategory: Endocrine investigation of interval clinical deterioration after an initially normal evaluation.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate ceiling: the changed phenotype narrows the axis, but the resident must still reject imaging stability and choose among endocrine assays. No claim of a difficult three-axis localization problem.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no preceding initial-DST feedback is visible.
checks.repairRecord: One revision replaces imaging foils with credible hormonal alternatives, corrects the unsupported repeat-washout history and separates reassessment from surgery. Stable reassessment concept retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Selects a familiar adrenal endocrine reassessment because the patient has treated hypertension.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Stable pressure on unchanged treatment and normal potassium do not explain the new cortisol-associated clinical pattern as a changed aldosterone phenotype.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: New resistant hypertension or unexplained hypokalemia would change the priority of aldosterone-renin reassessment.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats all interval adrenal concerns as renewed PPGL screening regardless of the changed phenotype.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The represented change is worsening diabetes with vertebral fragility, not a new episodic adrenergic course; cortisol reassessment best addresses it.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: New episodic adrenergic symptoms or a newly suspicious non-benign lesion could create a different metanephrine question.

parks.reason: Final author cue attack found that the preceding cortical-sparing explanation rehearsed the recurrence premise, and the offered lifelong-versus-symptoms/imaging policies were too easy. No routine resident difficulty or accepted basic exception is claimed.
unkeyedActions: Reauthor a distinct consequential long-term decision with credible same-stage alternatives and a decision-changing counterfactual.
Manager may assign a separate future clinic record review after finding a genuinely different interpretation objective.

options: Repeat AVS at an experienced center

No accepted foundational exception exists. Retain the supported safety fact unkeyed rather than claim a difficult two-step item or make an unsafe technique workaround.

Total removal versus preservation is preference-sensitive. A clinician must approve an exact balanced operative comparison before another scored version; no universal preference is keyed.

reviewRecords.title: Initial cortisol screen for an incidental adrenal lesion
fairness: DST is the defensible best option for the represented initial incidentaloma evaluation. Normal blood pressure/potassium and the unenhanced low-attenuation lesion help constrain the other hormonal axes; urinary free cortisol is a credible but weaker screen for subtle autonomy.

No decisive nonmedical wording shortcut identified. However, recognizing an incidentaloma and recalling its standard cortisol screen supplies the answer without consequential interpretation of the 4.2-cm/6-HU combination. Counting imaging recognition as a separate step overstates difficulty.

First node is coherent and self-contained; no later suppression result was used to judge it. The concept is high-yield resident knowledge, but this version does not meet the requested reasoning target.
suggestions: Build the decision around an actual interpretive obstacle, such as a documented prior screen whose acquisition or interval clinical course changes whether and how to repeat it; retain credible competing endocrine plans.

Alternatively seek explicit acceptance as foundational screening practice. Do not describe this exact version as moderate two-step reasoning merely because benign imaging and hormonal secretion are different concepts.

reviewRecords.title: Imaging follow-up of a homogeneous low-attenuation lesion
clarityIssues: 'Suppresses into the laboratory reference range' does not explicitly distinguish a post-dexamethasone suppression limit from an ordinary serum cortisol reference interval. This does not change the imaging key but should not teach that the intervals are interchangeable.
fairness: Homogeneity and 6 HU on the unenhanced acquisition support the keyed imaging plan under the guideline framework identified in the explanation. The size exceeding four centimeters provides a meaningful competing concern; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The later node remains interpretable with the initial presentation and update, but deleting the entire update leaves the imaging answer unchanged. Its position after DST adds chronology, not another consequential inference.

Both distractors seek additional characterization. Neither tests the especially plausible error of scheduling interval surveillance because of lesion size. The prior explanation distinguishes imaging from endocrine assessment without explicitly stating the follow-up key.
suggestions: Compare no further imaging with a concrete interval-surveillance plan and one credible additional-characterization plan; source any interval used.
Make this an independently framed imaging decision, or give it new acquisition/comparison information that actually changes the imaging conclusion rather than using a normal DST as its update.
If the cortisol result remains, identify it as below the laboratory's post-DST suppression limit.

reviewRecords.title: Confirmation of an abnormal incidentaloma cortisol screen
clarityIssues: The stem emphasizes absent dexamethasone exposure measurement, but the keyed label does not specify how validity of the repeated test will be assessed. Repeating an identical potentially confounded test is not necessarily a validity repair.

cues.phrase: The outside report contains no dexamethasone exposure measurement or basal ACTH result.
cues.why: Names the missing workup components immediately before the only option containing 'basal ACTH'; the learner can fill the named omission rather than interpret endocrine findings.

cues.phrase: Repeat overnight DST and measure basal ACTH
cues.why: The key uniquely combines a repeat of the named abnormal test with the explicitly missing measurement; the other options are single specialized tests.

fairness: Repeat confirmation with attention to test validity and ACTH independence is the defensible stage; the supplied record does not establish a need for high-dose DST or CRH testing.

An absent dexamethasone concentration is not by itself proof that the original test was invalid. No confident clinical error is asserted, but the text should distinguish missing information from demonstrated interference.
Standalone chronology is clear. The exact options mainly contrast a complete basic workup with premature specialized studies, leaving little resident-level competition.
suggestions: Replace the named-omission sentence with relevant observed administration, medication or acquisition details, supported by the existing clinical evidence process.

Give all alternatives comparable confirmation/etiology plans and specify the actual validity repair in the selected plan. Keep repeat confirmation and basal ACTH conceptually separate from automatic attribution to the visible nodule.

reviewRecords.title: Biochemical classification before choosing a cortisol source
fairness: Repeated concordant cortisol abnormalities and absence of exogenous exposure support moving to cause classification. Basal ACTH is the best offered next step before assigning significance to either anatomical focus.

Both imaging distractors are anchored to actual competing findings. The laboratory-versus-imaging distinction is clinically consequential, not a grammatical filter imposed by the task; no decisive nonmedical cue identified.

The two steps are recognizing sufficient evidence to pursue endogenous source evaluation and resisting two plausible imaging anchors until the ACTH pathway is established. Standalone presentation and task supply the needed context.
No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. This offline editorial PASS is not independent source verification or clinical approval.

reviewRecords.title: Operative target in overt adrenal cortisol excess

cues.phrase: a unilateral 3-cm homogeneous left adrenal lesion and a normal right gland
cues.why: Maps directly to the only unilateral left-sided operation. With no competing pituitary finding, ordinary lesion-removal logic can select the key without using ACTH. The observations are legitimate; the weak option set creates the shortcut.

fairness: The symptoms, repeated cortisol excess, suppressed ACTH and unilateral lesion support left adrenalectomy; no equally defensible offered alternative identified.

The normal opposite gland makes bilateral removal a weak distractor, and pituitary surgery lacks both biochemical and anatomical support. Deleting the cortisol/ACTH details still strongly points to the same option by the remaining anatomy and operative framing.
This is a coherent first part and a high-yield treatment principle, but the nominal classify-then-operate chain is not sustained by credible competitors.
suggestions: Make functional attribution consequential using genuinely competing anatomical findings or a different supported operative decision, with options representing close clinical errors.
Preserve the necessary localization facts; do not create difficulty by hiding the contralateral anatomy or suppressing essential ACTH information.

Use parallel specific regimens, such as hydrocortisone versus fludrocortisone versus no replacement, without inventing doses or recovery durations.
