The first node is coherent, but the mechanistic label and permission sentence supply the inference rather than testing it.
suggestions: Name the actual medication and show the relevant potassium and sampling record without calling the drug renin-raising.

State the actual potassium/medication correction in a concrete plan and compare credible alternative responses to the flawed screen. Preserve a real safety constraint only if it changes which plan is appropriate.

reviewRecords.title: Overt aldosterone phenotype and the next testing pathway
fairness: The prepared aldosterone/PRA results, spontaneous hypokalemia, resistant clinical phenotype and interest in surgery support the represented overt branch and subsequent functional lateralization. A routine suppression-first path and CT-directed surgery embody different credible errors.

The keyed pathway requires two consequential judgments: whether additional suppression is needed, then whether anatomical localization alone establishes the operative side. The three CT-containing plans do not create a unique majority-component key.

The repeat update changes the answer from the first node and provides meaningful progression. Prior feedback requires reliable biochemical diagnosis but does not disclose this overt-result exception. The later node is self-contained with its included presentation and update.

The exact assay-specific numerical exception is a current-guidance detail, not freshly verified in this no-network review. No confident inaccuracy identified; clinical sign-off should verify the stated threshold and assay pairing before release. High-yield status refers to the PA workup decision, not a claim that this exact numerical exception has measured exam frequency.

reviewRecords.title: Functional lateralization before aldosterone-directed surgery
fairness: AVS is the defensible best offered investigation for this 56-year-old operative candidate with confirmed primary aldosteronism. A unilateral nodule does not establish unilateral secretion.

Both alternatives merely further characterize an already imaged nodule. The key is the familiar named functional test; there is no new biochemical or acquisition conflict to resolve before choosing it.
No decisive nonmedical lexical cue identified. This is nevertheless predominantly a single workup-rule recall item, not two consequential steps. Its first-node chronology is coherent.
suggestions: Use a supported conflict in available localization evidence or adequacy that changes the next investigation, with genuinely competing localization plans.

Consider consolidating foundational AVS selection into feedback around the stronger later AVS interpretation task rather than scoring a separate routine recall node. Do not introduce an unsourced young-patient exception to manufacture difficulty.

reviewRecords.title: AVS lateralization opposite the visible adrenal nodule
fairness: The table supports the explanation's arithmetic: cortisol selectivity is 10 on the right and 20 on the left; aldosterone/cortisol is 6 versus 1, producing a lateralization ratio of 6. No arithmetic error identified.

Right adrenalectomy is the defensible best offered treatment given the stated desire for surgery, operative candidacy and functional localization. Left surgery follows the tempting anatomical nodule; medical treatment misses the supported operative opportunity but remains appropriate in a different preference or eligibility setting.

The learner must establish usable sampling, normalize secretion and reconcile a right functional source with a left anatomical finding. The explicit stimulated protocol and clearly separated values avoid a borderline-threshold dispute; no new cutoff is invented in this review.

The preceding AVS-selection explanation does not teach the calculation or its right-sided result. The later node progresses coherently and stands alone with the included presentation, update and exhibit. No decisive wording or component-convergence cue identified.

reviewRecords.title: Failed selective sampling before AVS lateralization
fairness: The right cortisol/peripheral ratio is 22/20 = 1.1, whereas the left is 400/20 = 20. The purported right sample does not support standard bilateral stimulated AVS interpretation. Repeating expert sampling is the best offered localization plan for a patient choosing surgery only after a unilateral source is demonstrated.

Using the aldosterone/cortisol ratios without checking selectivity could misleadingly appear to support the CT nodule. The two consequential steps are assessing sampling validity and determining whether the existing evidence can support a side-directed operation.
Both adrenal samples are neutrally labeled; 'Right-labeled sample' does not uniquely announce the invalid side because the left uses the same construction. No decisive nonmedical cue identified.

The standalone presentation, exhibit and task are coherent. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation appropriately limits its conclusion to standard bilateral interpretation rather than claiming that every incomplete AVS record is universally useless.

reviewRecords.title: Nonlateralizing aldosterone secretion despite a visible nodule

cues.phrase: Renal function and current potassium permit mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist treatment with monitoring.
cues.why: States eligibility for the keyed drug class and repeats its monitoring component. It replaces observed safety data with an answer-specific permission sentence.

fairness: The adequate bilateral selectivity and equal corrected secretion support medical treatment rather than unilateral adrenalectomy. Spironolactone with monitoring is the defensible best offered answer.

The computed ratios, experienced-center completeness label and explicit drug permission largely deliver both interpretation and management readiness. Right adrenalectomy has neither imaging nor functional support and is particularly weak.
The standalone case is coherent and the underlying concept is high-yield, but this exact wording permits answering without meaningful interpretation of the AVS data.
suggestions: Replace the permission sentence with concise actual potassium and renal-function observations, using supported values only where they matter.

Use raw or meaningfully conflicting localization information and a credible alternative management error; do not add calculations solely as busywork. Reconsider the unsupported right-sided operation as a distractor.

reviewRecords.title: Marginal metanephrine result with mismatched collection conditions

cues.phrase: collected seated during a painful visit and interpreted using a supine reference interval
cues.why: The explicit seated/supine mismatch is paired with 'Repeat plasma metanephrines under supine conditions' as the only corrective acquisition plan. A nonmedical reader can match the named mismatch to its repair. The necessary acquisition observations should remain; the alternatives need strengthening.

cues.phrase: Repeat whole-body FDG-PET/CT
cues.why: Repeats the already represented staging modality without a new acquisition or distribution question. Along with another anatomical scan, it leaves the key as the sole option addressing the newly described problem.

fairness: Standardized repeat biochemical testing is the defensible offered next investigation for a marginal result obtained under unsuitable comparison conditions. Cancer history and FDG uptake do not exclude a functional adrenal tumor.

The cancer/tissue decision supplies a meaningful clinical consequence, but the actual option set is dominated by two imaging plans that do not resolve the acquisition issue. The second step is not independently demanded by the choices.
First-node chronology is clear. The explanation's endocrine-safety wording also scaffolds the later biopsy task and must be included when judging that task's difficulty.
suggestions: Compare credible endocrine confirmation/acquisition plans at the same stage, with a supported patient-specific reason favoring one.

Retain the real collection and reference-interval facts rather than concealing the invalid comparison. Make the consequence for tissue sampling emerge from interpretation, not from unrelated completed-test foils.

reviewRecords.title: Biopsy decision after markedly abnormal standardized metanephrines

cues.phrase: FDG uptake and a cancer history do not settle the endocrine safety question.
cues.why: The preceding node's explanation explicitly teaches the same safety priority tested by the later biopsy-versus-endocrine-assessment task. This is a sequence cue, not leakage from the current node's post-answer explanation.

cues.phrase: Defer biopsy for endocrine tumor assessment
cues.why: It is the only cautious endocrine response, against two ways of performing the same challenged biopsy. The paired procedure distractors do not create two distinct credible competing decisions.

fairness: The markedly elevated values obtained under the laboratory protocol warrant endocrine evaluation before adrenal biopsy; changing needle technique does not resolve the concern. The intended key is defensible, and the explanation appropriately avoids claiming a universal numeric diagnostic threshold.

The update meaningfully changes the biochemical evidence, and a standalone learner can understand the decision with the included earlier presentation. In the full sequence, however, the prior safety explanation plus two near-equivalent biopsy distractors reduce it to a rehearsed recognition rule.
This is an important safety concept, but no separate accepted safety/onboarding exception is established by the presented question.
suggestions: Retain the safety facts and move this to an explicitly accepted foundational role, or redesign it to test a distinct remaining clinical decision after the first node's feedback.
Do not increase difficulty by hiding the abnormal biochemical result or implying a different needle makes an unevaluated functional tumor safe to biopsy.

reviewRecords.title: MEN2 cross-organ testing before thyroid surgery
fairness: Metanephrine assessment and calcium/PTH evaluation are the defensible offered plan for the RET-associated medullary carcinoma and stone history. Lack of classic spells does not remove the preoperative pheochromocytoma concern.
The four-option component matrix is balanced: each adrenal and companion-organ component appears twice. No unique convergence or length cue identified.

The task remains a syndrome-organ association recall item. Supplying medullary carcinoma plus RET effectively gives the syndrome; selecting its familiar screening panel is not two consequential steps simply because the panel includes two organs.
The first node is coherent and high-yield. Its explanation does not explicitly give the later operation-order answer.
suggestions: Use prior organ-specific results, acquisition limitations or a competing current clinical priority that changes the next required test, while preserving the essential preoperative safety screen.
Alternatively seek explicit foundational acceptance or merge the association teaching into the later operative-priority case. Keep the balanced option structure if a panel comparison remains.

reviewRecords.title: Operative order with competing MEN2 disease priorities
fairness: The repeated marked metanephrine elevations with an adrenal mass support addressing the functional adrenal tumor before elective thyroid or parathyroid intervention after appropriate preparation.

Node-positive medullary carcinoma is a credible competing priority. The patent airway and mild nonacute hypercalcemic course are necessary urgency information, not gratuitous negatives that should be removed to make the question harder.

The learner must interpret three organ-specific findings and rank their operative sequence despite an oncologically significant neck finding. The key is not the only named operation or the uniquely comprehensive plan.

The later update introduces the decisive functional results and urgency context. Earlier feedback names screening targets without stating the operative order; the node stands alone with its supplied presentation and update. No confident clinical inaccuracy or decisive nonmedical cue identified.

reviewRecords.title: Initial blockade for a functional adrenal tumor
fairness: Doxazosin is the defensible best initial oral agent among these options for a hypertensive patient with convincing catecholamine excess. Metoprolol before alpha blockade is inappropriate; labetalol is a credible mixed-blockade misconception rather than an equivalent initial dedicated alpha-blockade strategy.

The simultaneous hypertension and tachycardia create competing treatment impulses. The learner identifies the functional syndrome and chooses the safe initial receptor strategy despite the rate-control temptation.

All three labels are concise drug names, with no explanatory qualifiers or unique word overlap. 'No adrenergic preparation has begun' establishes the decision stage and does not uniquely repeat a drug name.

The first node is coherent and high-yield. Difficulty is at the lower end of moderate for a prepared resident, with the labetalol competitor carrying much of the discrimination. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

reviewRecords.title: Persistent tachycardia after alpha blockade
clarityIssues: The update gives neither the current pulse nor an actual blood pressure, although it replaces the initial 174/102 and 108/min findings with 'low-normal' pressure and persistent tachycardia. Severity and hemodynamic tolerance matter to whether further medication is appropriate.
The supplied update establishes sinus rhythm but does not show the clinical importance of the remaining tachycardia. Do not silently reuse the initial pulse as the new post-treatment value.
fairness: Adding beta blockade while continuing established alpha blockade is the defensible intended strategy if persistent tachycardia warrants treatment and the current pressure tolerates it. Increasing alpha blockade at low-normal pressure or removing alpha protection are weaker choices.

The two consequential steps can be present: interpret the response and assess other causes, then select additive rate control while maintaining vascular protection. However, the current qualitative observations leave the severity/tolerance boundary less clear than the confident explanation implies.

The later node follows coherently and can stand alone with its presentation and update. Prior feedback teaches initial alpha blockade but does not explicitly give this subsequent medication change. No decisive nonmedical lexical cue identified; the concern is missing clinical specificity, not a confident claim that beta blockade is wrong.
suggestions: Supply actual repeat pulse/BP observations and any relevant ongoing symptoms so the learner can distinguish clinically important residual tachycardia from a finding that merits observation or further assessment.
Keep the negative evaluation concise and retain only alternatives that genuinely compete at the observed treatment stage. Do not invent a universal heart-rate or blood-pressure cutoff.

reviewRecords.title: Cortical preservation in the only remaining adrenal gland
clarityIssues: 'Which operation should be offered ... after discussion' does not establish the patient's priority after that discussion. More than one operation can reasonably be offered in a preference-sensitive decision.

cues.phrase: an experienced adrenal surgeon finds complete removal without capsule disruption feasible while retaining cortex
cues.why: Gives an expert feasibility conclusion that nearly paraphrases 'Cortical-sparing right adrenalectomy.' It supplies the judgment the learner is nominally asked to make.

cues.phrase: a substantial rim of cortex
cues.why: Reinforces the cortex-preservation wording unique to the key, especially when paired with the explicit expert endorsement. Anatomy is needed, but the additional conclusion turns it into answer rehearsal.

fairness: Cortical-sparing surgery is a reasonable operation to offer in this hereditary remaining-gland setting, and the explanation correctly avoids promising steroid independence.

Total adrenalectomy remains a defensible alternative for a patient who prioritizes avoiding remnant recurrence and accepts lifelong replacement. The visible task and patient information do not resolve that tradeoff sufficiently to make 'should be offered' uniquely select one operation.

Percutaneous ablation is a weak peer to the two established surgical choices in this resectable case. The apparent difficulty comes partly from an unresolved preference-sensitive ranking, not valid two-step reasoning.
The standalone chronology is coherent. This is a high-yield hereditary endocrine tradeoff, but no confident claim is made that one universal operative policy applies.
suggestions: Ask a precisely bounded question about which operation can achieve complete tumor removal while offering a chance of retained endogenous steroid production, or provide a balanced, decision-relevant patient preference that resolves the recurrence-versus-replacement tradeoff.

Replace the pre-answer expert endorsement with necessary observed anatomy and preserve any genuine oncologic constraint. Use feedback to explain feasibility, recurrence and possible steroid dependence.
Have the clinician confirm the exact operative comparison; do not key a universal preference-sensitive choice simply because cortical-sparing surgery is feasible.

reviewRecords.title: Management pathway for a suspicious primary adrenal malignancy
clarityIssues: 'Hormonal evaluation, including metanephrines, has been completed' gives completion status rather than results. This does not invalidate expert referral, but leaves the endocrine context incompletely specified for the linked operative pathway.

cues.phrase: Expert adrenal oncology assessment for resection
cues.why: The only broad expert-assessment plan is compared with committing to a needle procedure or surveillance for a large irregular possibly invasive mass. Generic caution and the conspicuously aggressive imaging description favor the key before the specific biopsy principle must be known.

fairness: Expert oncologic resection assessment is the defensible offered pathway. Routine adrenal biopsy is not required to establish a resectable suspected primary cortical malignancy, and surveillance is poorly supported by the represented morphology.

The absence of another cancer and negative distant staging support the intended primary-adrenal context. Nevertheless, the choices mainly contrast sensible specialist assessment with two weak plans, rather than a close resident-level decision.
The first node is coherent. Its explanation points toward resection but does not explicitly disclose the later open en bloc operative technique. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: State the clinically relevant hormonal results, without treating 'completed' as equivalent to normal or adequately prepared.
Compare concrete plausible oncologic evaluation/resection pathways at the same decision stage, using the primary-versus-metastatic or resectability context to determine the answer.
Remove the generic expert-assessment advantage without replacing it with an unsupported obligatory biopsy.

reviewRecords.title: Operative plan for adrenal tumor invading the kidney

cues.phrase: the involved adrenal-kidney tissue can be removed together
cues.why: Translates directly into 'Open en bloc adrenal and involved renal resection.' The update gives the operative solution as an expert feasibility statement instead of leaving a meaningful planning inference.

cues.phrase: Priya can undergo the proposed operation.
cues.why: An unnamed 'proposed operation' has effectively just been described as combined removal. This permission sentence endorses that plan before the options.

fairness: For the represented localized resectable invasive tumor, complete intact en bloc removal of involved tissue is the defensible offered goal. Separating an invaded plane or deliberately debulking potentially completely resectable disease are inferior alternatives.

The update does change contact into confirmed invasion, and the sequence is coherent. However, it then supplies the operative consequence. The later task stands alone with its context but tests matching an already stated plan.
The earlier resection explanation further weakens the debulking foil. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation appropriately distinguishes actual invasion from mere abutment.
suggestions: Retain evidence distinguishing actual invasion from contact and remove the sentence prescribing combined removal plus the vague feasibility endorsement.
Use credible competing operative plans whose ranking depends on observed invasion, intact removal and resectability. Keep relevant operative fitness information factual if it changes the choice.
Do not turn mere contact into a universal nephrectomy rule when rewriting the case.

reviewRecords.title: Management after interval growth of an indeterminate adrenal lesion
fairness: The arithmetic is correct: 38 minus 30 is 8 mm, and 8/30 is approximately 27%. The observations exceed both growth components described in the explanation over the represented nine-month interval.

The learner must interpret relative and absolute growth using comparable measurements, then decide whether the previously chosen surveillance plan remains appropriate. Expert resection reassessment is the defensible offered response; growth itself is not proof of malignancy.

The established surveillance decision is a credible inertia trap. The task does not call the growth 'significant' or name a crossed threshold, so the conclusion is not supplied before answering. The standalone chronology is clear.

The exact guideline criterion has not been freshly source-verified under the no-network constraint; no confident error is identified. This is a clinical growth-management question, so the statistics single-skill exception does not apply merely because a percentage is computed.

reviewRecords.title: Hormonal reassessment despite stable benign adrenal imaging
clarityIssues: 'Repeat adrenal washout CT' presumes a prior washout study, whereas the supplied prior/current imaging description only establishes an unenhanced CT. This is a minor but avoidable chronology mismatch.

cues.phrase: Her homogeneous 2-cm adrenal nodule remains unchanged at 7 HU on unenhanced CT.
cues.why: Stable imaging is contrasted with worsening metabolic findings, but the key is the only hormonal test and both distractors pursue anatomy/malignancy. The structure allows a test-category shortcut instead of choosing among credible endocrine investigations. The imaging facts themselves are necessary and should remain.

fairness: Repeat cortisol assessment is the defensible best offered investigation when relevant comorbidities worsen after an initially normal adrenal evaluation. Stable benign morphology does not exclude newly relevant hormonal activity.

Whole-body PET/CT and another characterization CT are weak competitors in the explicitly unchanged low-attenuation lesion. The clinical change is consequential in principle, but this option set does not require a second substantive inference.
The standalone time course is otherwise clear. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified in the key or the explanation's statement that a subsequent result would not automatically mandate surgery.
suggestions: Compare credible endocrine reassessment strategies or actual alternative explanations using patient-specific observations that resolve the choice.
Keep stable imaging as the competing reassurance signal, but replace imaging-only foils and correct the unsupported 'Repeat' washout history.
Preserve the distinction between deciding to reassess hormone secretion and deciding on surgery.

definitions.name: Nora Ellis
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 52-year-old woman, attends the clinic after a kidney-stone CT shows a homogeneous 4.2-cm adrenal lesion measuring 6 HU on the unenhanced series. Blood pressure and potassium are within their reference ranges. She reports no bruising or proximal weakness.

nodes.objective: Separate benign adrenal morphology from the need to evaluate occult cortisol secretion.
nodes.stem: Which endocrine evaluation should Nora Ellis receive for this incidental adrenal lesion?

choices.label: 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test
choices.rationale: Benign lipid-rich morphology does not establish normal cortisol secretion; this is the incidentaloma cortisol screen.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes anatomical reassurance from endocrine reassurance.
choices.counterfactual: Frail limited-life-expectancy circumstances could favor omitting this screen.

choices.label: Twenty-four-hour urinary free cortisol measurement
choices.rationale: This is useful in overt Cushing evaluation but is less suitable than DST for subtle incidentaloma-associated cortisol autonomy.
choices.temptation: Selects a familiar test for overt cortisol excess.
choices.counterfactual: Progressive overt cortisol-excess features could make urine free cortisol part of diagnostic confirmation.

choices.label: Clinical review without further endocrine testing
choices.rationale: Low attenuation addresses malignancy risk, not occult cortisol activity.
choices.temptation: Treats a benign-looking scan as a nonfunctioning-gland result.
choices.counterfactual: An already normal initial endocrine evaluation with unchanged clinical status would support no routine retesting.

nodes.explanation: Interpret the low unenhanced attenuation as an imaging finding, then assess the separate endocrine question. An overnight 1-mg DST is the recommended cortisol screen for this incidentaloma. Urinary free cortisol addresses overt hypercortisolism better than subtle autonomy.

steps: Recognize lipid-rich benign imaging without equating it to absence of secretion.
Choose the incidentaloma cortisol screen rather than an overt-syndrome test or no evaluation.
reasoning.closestError: Omit endocrine workup because the lesion measures 6 HU.
reasoning.decidingObservation: This is the initial endocrine evaluation, with benign morphology but no cortisol result.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the initial endocrine evaluation were normal and the clinical course unchanged, no routine repeat endocrine testing would be appropriate.
reasoning.deletionTest: HU/acquisition separates imaging risk from hormonal activity; blood pressure/potassium constrain competing axes; absent overt signs distinguish subtle autonomy from overt workup. Kidney-stone imaging establishes incidental discovery. The exact age is fixed editorial context.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed the former list of no-frailty/no-virilization exclusions. All options are actual endocrine evaluation plans; no wording names a catecholamine hazard. The test name is necessarily specific, so difficulty rests on imaging versus physiology rather than lexical disguise.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Initial outpatient endocrine assessment; three specific testing or no-retest plans.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate, at the easier end of this packet; low-HU reassurance is the credible error. Requires independent difficulty review, with no claimed basic exception.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node; no future DST result visible. Feedback does not state the later imaging follow-up answer.
reasoning.repairRecord: New exact version replaces the four-way assay recall item with the imaging-versus-endocrine decision and a credible no-testing competitor.

nodes.objective: Apply unenhanced morphology rather than size in deciding additional adrenal imaging after a normal endocrine evaluation.
nodes.currentUpdate: Nora's cortisol suppresses into the laboratory reference range on the correctly completed DST. Her blood pressure, potassium and clinical examination remain unchanged.
nodes.stem: Which adrenal imaging plan should Nora Ellis receive after this evaluation?

choices.label: No additional adrenal-specific imaging
choices.rationale: The homogeneous 6-HU unenhanced lesion meets the current benign-imaging criterion despite its size.
choices.temptation: Applies acquisition and morphology rather than the historical size shortcut.
choices.counterfactual: Heterogeneity or indeterminate unenhanced attenuation would require a different pathway.

choices.label: Dedicated adrenal washout CT
choices.rationale: An unequivocally lipid-rich lesion is already characterized; washout adds no needed classification here.
choices.temptation: Escalates because the lesion is larger than four centimeters.
choices.counterfactual: An indeterminate lesion above the benign attenuation range could require additional characterization.

choices.label: Adrenal chemical-shift MRI
choices.rationale: A second characterization modality is unnecessary for the supplied unenhanced benign pattern.
choices.temptation: Uses a different modality to compensate for the lesion's size.
choices.counterfactual: A lesion not conclusively characterized on CT may merit another modality after expert assessment.

nodes.explanation: The deciding combination is homogeneity plus 6 HU on an unenhanced acquisition. Under ESE 2023 that pattern does not require more adrenal imaging solely because the diameter exceeds four centimeters. A normal hormonal evaluation answers a separate axis.

steps: Distinguish a true low-HU unenhanced benign pattern from an indeterminate mass.
Reject size-driven repeat characterization after the separate endocrine assessment is normal.
reasoning.closestError: Order washout CT because the lesion exceeds four centimeters.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Homogeneous 6-HU unenhanced morphology, not a contrast-phase attenuation.
reasoning.counterfactual: Changing the unenhanced lesion to heterogeneous 28 HU removes reassurance and requires expert characterization/surgical assessment.
reasoning.deletionTest: The update earns a decision by closing the hormone-excess axis before surveillance; size creates the historical-rule competitor. Unenhanced acquisition is essential.
reasoning.cueAttack: No task term matches only the key. Three actual imaging policies; the no-imaging option is short but not uniquely cautious. Prior feedback covers hormonal screening, not the no-imaging rule.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Additional adrenal imaging policy after initial evaluation.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate because an old size criterion competes with current morphology-based guidance.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: The earlier screen explanation deliberately omits imaging follow-up recommendations. The update is needed to close the endocrine axis.
reasoning.repairRecord: Authored a distinct follow-up objective instead of another cosmetic DST variant.

definitions.name: Elena Shaw
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 59-year-old woman, attends the clinic with a homogeneous 2.6-cm adrenal nodule. A single overnight DST left serum cortisol above the laboratory suppression limit. She has diabetes but no proximal weakness or easy bruising. The outside report contains no dexamethasone exposure measurement or basal ACTH result.

nodes.objective: Validate persistent cortisol nonsuppression and ACTH independence before attributing an incidentaloma and choosing surgery.
nodes.stem: Which outpatient endocrine testing plan should Elena Shaw receive next?

choices.label: Repeat overnight DST and measure basal ACTH
choices.rationale: Repeat the abnormal screen with attention to test validity and establish the ACTH relationship before treatment attribution.
choices.temptation: Validates the biochemical phenotype instead of assuming the nodule is the source.
choices.counterfactual: Repeated valid abnormal testing with already suppressed ACTH would allow source-directed assessment rather than repeating this stage.

choices.label: Perform high-dose dexamethasone suppression testing
choices.rationale: A specialized etiologic maneuver does not replace confirmation and initial ACTH assessment.
choices.temptation: Moves directly into familiar Cushing localization maneuvers.
choices.counterfactual: A selected ACTH-dependent workup under specialist direction could use a different etiologic pathway.

choices.label: Perform corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation testing
choices.rationale: This is premature before the basal pathway and validity of cortisol autonomy have been established.
choices.temptation: Treats nonsuppression as established ACTH-dependent disease.
choices.counterfactual: Selected ACTH-dependent diagnostic uncertainty after basal classification could warrant specialized testing.

nodes.explanation: One abnormal incidentaloma screen does not prove that the visible nodule causes clinically important cortisol excess. Recheck the suppression result and its validity, and determine basal ACTH before assigning the source. This node selects the diagnostic stage, not adrenalectomy.

steps: Distinguish an abnormal screening observation from a persistent, attributed functional diagnosis.
Select repeat valid suppression assessment plus basal ACTH instead of specialized ACTH-dependent localization tests.
reasoning.closestError: Treat a single abnormal DST as sufficient endocrine attribution.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Only one nonsuppression result is available and ACTH has not been measured.
reasoning.counterfactual: With repeated valid cortisol abnormalities and suppressed ACTH already documented, source-directed adrenal assessment becomes appropriate.
reasoning.deletionTest: Single-test chronology, absent basal ACTH and the actual test record all establish the unresolved stage. Diabetes makes the eventual consequence relevant but does not itself choose surgery.
reasoning.cueAttack: The absent-result statement supplies necessary acquisition history; competing tests are all equally concrete endocrine investigations. It does not say 'repeat is needed' or name ACTH independence in the task.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Next endocrine investigation plan; all options are named testing plans.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard because incidental-image anchoring and premature specialized testing are credible errors.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no prior feedback states its diagnostic answer.
reasoning.repairRecord: Explicit new meaning expands the older basal-ACTH-only objective to validation and attribution; no old history is transferred.

definitions.name: Maya Kent
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 43-year-old woman, attends the clinic for endocrine-surgery evaluation. Repeat late-night salivary cortisol and urine free cortisol exceed their laboratory decision limits. Medication review finds no glucocorticoid exposure. A prior contrast abdominal CT describes a small left adrenal nodule; an earlier headache MRI describes a small pituitary focus.

nodes.objective: Interpret concordant cortisol abnormalities and use ACTH to classify the source pathway before anchoring on incidental images.
nodes.stem: Which investigation should guide the next source evaluation for Maya Kent's cortisol findings?

choices.label: Basal plasma ACTH measurement
choices.rationale: Concordant cortisol evidence warrants cause classification; the basal ACTH relationship determines which anatomical pathway to pursue.
choices.temptation: Uses physiology before competing incidental images.
choices.counterfactual: If ACTH were already classified on adequate repeat samples, source-directed imaging would replace this stage.

choices.label: Dedicated pituitary MRI
choices.rationale: The small pituitary focus does not establish an ACTH source without biochemical classification.
choices.temptation: Anchors on an existing pituitary image.
choices.counterfactual: An established ACTH-dependent pathway could warrant pituitary-directed investigation.

choices.label: Dedicated adrenal CT
choices.rationale: The incidental adrenal nodule is not proof of autonomous cortisol secretion.
choices.temptation: Anchors on the incidental adrenal nodule.
choices.counterfactual: Suppressed ACTH on valid sampling would direct adrenal evaluation.

nodes.explanation: First interpret the repeated concordant cortisol results as a reason to classify the cause. Then use basal ACTH before selecting between competing anatomical findings. Neither small image establishes functional attribution.

steps: Recognize concordant repeated cortisol abnormalities without an exogenous exposure explanation.
Choose biochemical source classification before either incidental-image pathway.
reasoning.closestError: Order pituitary MRI because an earlier scan already showed a focus.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The two images compete, while no basal ACTH classification is supplied.
reasoning.counterfactual: With suppressed ACTH already established on valid repeat sampling, adrenal-directed imaging becomes the appropriate branch.
reasoning.deletionTest: Both cortisol modalities establish the stage; exposure review preserves the endogenous boundary; the two incidental images create genuine competing source anchors.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed 'endogenous Cushing already established' and 'classify etiologic pathway' from the old lead-in. All choices are specific investigations and none is uniquely comprehensive.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: First etiologic investigation after concordant cortisol evidence.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate because both images can attract a resident who localizes before classifying.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Standalone. The preserved B2A11 source-imaging PASS remains a separate case; this feedback must not be placed immediately before it without renewed context review.
reasoning.repairRecord: Changed raw evidence and real anatomical competitors, preserving the ACTH-classification concept. Removed a four-sibling cosmetic repeat pattern.

definitions.name: Clara West
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 46-year-old woman, attends the clinic with progressive proximal weakness, easy bruising and worsening diabetes. Repeated cortisol studies exceed their laboratory decision limits; ACTH is repeatedly below the assay reporting limit. Medication review finds no glucocorticoid exposure. Adrenal-protocol CT shows a unilateral 3-cm homogeneous left adrenal lesion and a normal right gland. She has chosen operative treatment after endocrine assessment.

nodes.objective: Use concordant hormonal source attribution and unilateral anatomy to choose the operation for overt adrenal cortisol excess.
nodes.stem: Which operation should be planned for Clara West's cortisol disorder?

choices.label: Laparoscopic left adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: The overt phenotype, suppressed ACTH and unilateral adrenal anatomy support removing the left adrenal source.
choices.temptation: Integrates functional and anatomical attribution.
choices.counterfactual: If cortisol excess were ACTH-dependent, treating the ACTH source would take priority.

choices.label: Laparoscopic bilateral adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: The supplied anatomy and biochemistry do not justify removing a normal contralateral gland.
choices.temptation: Confuses all cortisol excess with a bilateral adrenal target.
choices.counterfactual: Refractory ACTH-dependent cortisol excess or selected bilateral adrenal disease can require a different operative strategy.

choices.label: Transsphenoidal pituitary adenomectomy
choices.rationale: Suppressed ACTH does not support a pituitary-driven cortisol source.
choices.temptation: Treats the common pituitary pathway despite discordant physiology.
choices.counterfactual: A supported pituitary ACTH source would change the surgical target.

nodes.explanation: The cortisol results and suppressed ACTH must agree with the operative target. Here the overt cortisol phenotype and unilateral left adrenal lesion support unilateral adrenalectomy. The normal contralateral gland does not justify bilateral removal.

steps: Interpret cortisol excess with suppressed ACTH as an adrenal source pathway.
Use unilateral anatomy and the established operative goal to select left rather than bilateral or pituitary surgery.
reasoning.closestError: Choose a pituitary operation from the common Cushing association.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Repeatedly suppressed ACTH with a unilateral left lesion and normal right adrenal anatomy.
reasoning.counterfactual: Changing ACTH to an established pituitary-dependent pattern changes the source operation; changing the anatomy to bilateral disease removes this unilateral key.
reasoning.deletionTest: Symptoms establish overt disease rather than the disputed MACS branch; hormonal chronology supports attribution; laterality selects the operation; the patient's operative choice fixes the treatment stage.
reasoning.cueAttack: Three specific operations, similar label lengths. The known decision to operate is common background, not a key-only permission. No gland is called 'causal' before answering.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Definitive source operation, not further investigation versus treatment.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate: a resident must integrate physiology and anatomy without treating every cortisol syndrome identically.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node; no postoperative result is shown. Feedback does not teach steroid replacement.
reasoning.repairRecord: New overt-disease decision avoids making a disputed universal MACS operative recommendation.

nodes.objective: Account for contralateral axis suppression after unilateral surgery for overt cortisol excess.
nodes.currentUpdate: At follow-up, the founder reviews Clara's outside-hospital record after left adrenalectomy. The right adrenal gland was preserved. The inpatient team asks what adrenal replacement plan should accompany recovery from the operation.
nodes.stem: Which adrenal replacement plan should be recommended in Clara West's discharge record?

choices.label: Glucocorticoid replacement pending axis recovery
choices.rationale: Chronic cortisol excess suppresses the remaining axis; anatomical preservation does not establish immediate glucocorticoid sufficiency.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes residual gland anatomy from its current function.
choices.counterfactual: After documented axis recovery, replacement can be withdrawn under endocrine guidance.

choices.label: Mineralocorticoid replacement pending axis recovery
choices.rationale: The expected suppression concerns ACTH-driven cortisol secretion, not loss of both mineralocorticoid-producing glands.
choices.temptation: Treats all postoperative adrenal disorders as complete primary adrenal failure.
choices.counterfactual: Bilateral total adrenalectomy or mineralocorticoid-deficient primary adrenal failure would change replacement needs.

choices.label: No adrenal replacement after unilateral surgery
choices.rationale: The normal-appearing remaining gland may be functionally suppressed after overt cortisol excess.
choices.temptation: Equates preservation of one adrenal with immediate endocrine reserve.
choices.counterfactual: An endocrine evaluation documenting adequate postoperative cortisol reserve after non-cortisol surgery would support a different plan.

nodes.explanation: After removing an overt cortisol-secreting source, the preserved gland and pituitary drive may still be suppressed. Provide glucocorticoid replacement and endocrine follow-up until axis recovery is documented. Unilateral surgery does not imply lifelong mineralocorticoid replacement.

steps: Infer functional suppression of the remaining axis from the prior overt cortisol exposure.
Select glucocorticoid replacement despite preserved contralateral anatomy.
reasoning.closestError: Omit replacement because the right adrenal gland was preserved.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The operation treated overt autonomous cortisol excess, rather than a nonfunctioning nodule.
reasoning.counterfactual: With documented recovery of adrenal cortisol reserve, the need for ongoing glucocorticoid replacement changes.
reasoning.deletionTest: Prior overt disease, actual unilateral procedure and remaining-gland anatomy all determine replacement. The outside chart frame locates inpatient care correctly.
reasoning.cueAttack: The update does not call the gland suppressed or announce a steroid need. Every option is an adrenal replacement plan. No doses or invented recovery timeline are used.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Postoperative discharge adrenal replacement plan.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: preserved anatomy is a plausible trap when endocrine feedback is missed.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: The first explanation addresses source selection only. The new postoperative state requires a separate endocrine consequence, not repetition of laterality.
reasoning.repairRecord: Outside-hospital care is reviewed in clinic using the existing setting; no new ICU runtime is proposed.

definitions.name: David Marsh
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 51-year-old man, attends the clinic with hypertension despite several agents. Potassium was low before any diuretic prescription. An outside aldosterone-renin screen was called negative, but potassium remained below the reference range during sampling and the medication record included a renin-raising diuretic. The treating clinician can safely revise the regimen for repeat assessment.

nodes.objective: Recognize an unreliable negative aldosterone-renin screen and repeat it after safe potassium and medication preparation.
nodes.stem: Which endocrine testing plan should David Marsh receive next?

choices.label: Repeat aldosterone and renin after preparation
choices.rationale: Low potassium and medication effects can obscure the phenotype; the negative screen does not settle this high-suspicion evaluation.
choices.temptation: Reassesses test validity before abandoning the endocrine pathway.
choices.counterfactual: An adequately prepared negative evaluation with low clinical suspicion would not require this specific repeat.

choices.label: Proceed to saline suppression testing
choices.rationale: Suppression testing does not repair the inadequately prepared initial screen.
choices.temptation: Skips validation and moves directly to confirmatory testing.
choices.counterfactual: An adequately prepared intermediate-probability positive screen in a surgical candidate can prompt specialist suppression assessment.

choices.label: Proceed to CT and adrenal venous sampling
choices.rationale: Lateralization is premature before the biochemical evaluation is interpretable.
choices.temptation: Uses an invasive localization pathway to resolve an unreliable screen.
choices.counterfactual: Confirmed PA in a suitable adult who wants surgery supports CT plus AVS.

nodes.explanation: The negative label is weaker than the acquisition record. Potassium and interfering medications must be handled safely before interpreting a repeat aldosterone-renin screen. Localization does not substitute for a reliable biochemical diagnosis.

steps: Recognize that the original low-potassium phenotype predates the diuretic and remains clinically suspicious.
Identify the sampling confounders and repeat prepared biochemistry instead of treating the report label as exclusion.
reasoning.closestError: Accept the outside negative label or jump directly to AVS.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Low potassium and a renin-raising medication were present during the negative screen.
reasoning.counterfactual: With valid prepared overt positive results and surgical intent, localization rather than another screen is appropriate.
reasoning.deletionTest: Prediuretic chronology prevents attributing all hypokalemia to medication; sampling conditions invalidate the result. Safe medication revision is necessary because blanket withdrawal is not taught.
reasoning.cueAttack: The task does not name the omitted preparation. Every option is an endocrine testing pathway with timing metadata. The key is no longer a generic 'individualized evaluation'.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Next endocrine testing pathway after an unreliable result.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted hard: test validity competes with a superficially reassuring report and a high-suspicion phenotype.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node. Feedback does not give the overt-phenotype cutoff or state the next node's key.
reasoning.repairRecord: Explicitly versioned the changed objective from selecting ARR to repairing invalid acquisition; old FSRS history remains with the prior concept.

nodes.objective: Apply the overt renin-independent phenotype boundary before localization for surgery.
nodes.currentUpdate: After potassium correction and safe medication adjustment, David has morning seated testing without dietary sodium restriction. Immunoassay aldosterone is 28 ng/dL and plasma renin activity is 0.1 ng/mL/h. He wants adrenal surgery if unilateral disease can be established.
nodes.stem: Which testing pathway should David Marsh follow after these repeat results?

choices.label: Adrenal CT with adrenal venous sampling
choices.rationale: The resistant-hypertension/hypokalemia phenotype with these prepared results meets the narrow overt branch; separate suppression is not required.
choices.temptation: Applies the exception while preserving functional lateralization.
choices.counterfactual: An intermediate-probability prepared positive screen can require suppression assessment before surgery eligibility.

choices.label: Saline suppression followed by adrenal CT
choices.rationale: It adds mandatory suppression where the represented overt branch does not require it.
choices.temptation: Uses a universal positive-screen confirmation rule.
choices.counterfactual: Less overt biochemistry in a surgical candidate can justify a specialist suppression test.

choices.label: Adrenal CT for nodule-directed surgery
choices.rationale: Bypassing suppression here does not mean bypassing functional lateralization.
choices.temptation: Converts a strong biochemical diagnosis into CT-only side selection.
choices.counterfactual: A narrowly selected very young patient may be considered for a different AVS pathway; this 51-year-old is outside that exception.

nodes.explanation: These are prepared results in resistant hypertension with spontaneous hypokalemia: immunoassay aldosterone exceeds 20 ng/dL and PRA is below 0.2 ng/mL/h. The documented overt branch does not require a separate suppression test. CT plus AVS still addresses the separate question of which gland produces excess aldosterone.

steps: Interpret the prepared values together with the prediuretic hypokalemia and resistant hypertension.
Apply the narrow no-suppression branch while retaining functional lateralization before choosing surgery.
reasoning.closestError: Order saline suppression for every positive aldosterone-renin screen.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Prepared immunoassay aldosterone 28 ng/dL and PRA 0.1 ng/mL/h with the overt clinical phenotype.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the prepared aldosterone result were intermediate rather than overt, the blanket bypass conclusion would no longer follow.
reasoning.deletionTest: Acquisition, assay, units, phenotype and operative intent all set the guideline branch. No calculated ARR is repeated as a decorative extra value.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed the old exhibit's conclusion 'overt renin-independent excess'. Three actual pathways have comparable labels; no unique explanation is embedded in the key.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Next endocrine testing pathway for a surgical candidate.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted hard: confirmation and lateralization are distinct decisions even when one step can be bypassed.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback concerns validity only. New valid numbers change the branch; earlier negative results are not used as current evidence.
reasoning.repairRecord: Reused N1 concept meaning, replaced its cue-heavy phenotype summary with raw prepared observations and narrowed the task.

definitions.name: Owen Price
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 56-year-old man, attends the clinic with biochemically confirmed primary aldosteronism after prepared endocrine testing. CT shows a 1.7-cm left adrenal nodule and no right nodule. He wishes to pursue surgery. Cortisol suppresses within the laboratory range after DST.

nodes.objective: Distinguish CT anatomy from functional lateralization in an adult surgical candidate.
nodes.stem: Which investigation should guide the side of Owen Price's aldosterone-directed operation?

choices.label: CT review with adrenal venous sampling
choices.rationale: A unilateral nodule in this age group does not establish unilateral hormone production; functional lateralization is needed.
choices.temptation: Separates visible anatomy from functional secretion.
choices.counterfactual: A narrowly selected very young patient with marked PA may follow an exception; this patient is not represented by it.

choices.label: Adrenal chemical-shift MRI
choices.rationale: Another morphological study does not identify which gland produces the excess aldosterone.
choices.temptation: Treats better nodule characterization as functional proof.
choices.counterfactual: An indeterminate anatomical lesion could require MRI for a different imaging objective.

choices.label: Dedicated adrenal washout CT
choices.rationale: Washout addresses lesion characterization, not functional side selection.
choices.temptation: Uses a familiar adrenal imaging protocol to solve a biochemical lateralization problem.
choices.counterfactual: Indeterminate adrenal morphology may warrant additional characterization independently of PA lateralization.

nodes.explanation: The left-sided nodule is anatomical evidence. In this adult who wants surgery, CT assessment plus AVS is the usual pathway for identifying unilateral secretion. Additional nodule imaging does not answer the same functional question.

steps: Recognize that a unilateral CT nodule may not be the aldosterone source.
Choose functional lateralization before selecting an operative side in an older surgical candidate.
reasoning.closestError: Treat the left CT nodule as proof of left-sided secretion.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Age 56 and a surgical decision with a unilateral image but no functional side result.
reasoning.counterfactual: If adequate AVS already demonstrated unilateral secretion, another localization study would be unnecessary before operative planning.
reasoning.deletionTest: Age avoids the very-young exception; CT laterality creates the anchor; operative intent makes AVS relevant. The cortisol result is retained for the subsequent AVS normalization assumption.
reasoning.cueAttack: Three named investigations, no 'CT alone' caricature. The key is a concrete test, not a comprehensive information-gathering slogan.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Functional side-selection investigation.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate: deciding the investigation requires separating anatomy and secretion.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Feedback does not teach the numerical selectivity or lateralization formula used by the next node.
reasoning.repairRecord: Removed preinterpreted ARR and the repeated four-sibling overt-label exhibit; the new task concentrates on the actual side-selection uncertainty.

nodes.objective: Normalize technically adequate AVS measurements and choose the functional side despite a contralateral CT nodule.
nodes.currentUpdate: Owen's simultaneous cosyntropin-stimulated AVS record is now available. He remains an operative candidate. The left adrenal nodule is unchanged.

exhibit.caption: Constructed patient record; values are fictional observations.

nodes.stem: Which aldosterone-directed treatment should be recommended for Owen Price after expert review of this AVS record?

choices.label: Right adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: Both veins are selective; corrected ratios are right 6 and left 1, supporting right lateralization despite the left nodule.
choices.temptation: Integrates technical validity, normalization and the side conflict.
choices.counterfactual: Reversing the corrected ratio dominance would reverse the operative side.

choices.label: Left adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: The image is on the left, but the corrected secretory ratio is much higher on the right.
choices.temptation: Chooses the visible nodule instead of the functional result.
choices.counterfactual: A valid left-dominant corrected AVS ratio would support left adrenalectomy.

choices.label: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist therapy
choices.rationale: Medical therapy remains an option, but a patient who chose surgery has a supported unilateral functional target here.
choices.temptation: Treats discordance with CT as automatically bilateral disease.
choices.counterfactual: Bilateral nonlateralizing AVS or a decision against surgery would favor targeted medical treatment.

nodes.explanation: Cortisol selectivity ratios are right 10 and left 20. Aldosterone/cortisol ratios are right 6 and left 1; the lateralization ratio is 6. The functional target is the right gland despite the left CT nodule. This is not a guarantee of cure.

steps: Check bilateral sampling adequacy and normalize aldosterone to cortisol rather than comparing raw concentration or CT nodules.
Use the right-to-left corrected ratio of six and the patient's operative choice to select right adrenalectomy.
reasoning.closestError: Operate on the left CT nodule.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Both samples are selective and the corrected secretory ratio is sixfold higher on the right.
reasoning.counterfactual: Change right aldosterone to 200 and left aldosterone to 2400 ng/dL with cortisol unchanged: corrected ratios become right 1 and left 6, reversing the operative side.
reasoning.deletionTest: Every table cell contributes to selectivity or normalization. Cosyntropin and prior normal cortisol screening fix the interpretation assumptions. The CT side is the competing anchor.
reasoning.cueAttack: The table does not print ratios or a laterality interpretation. Options are comparable treatment choices. No raw 'high' label appears beside the correct gland.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Aldosterone-directed treatment after completed functional localization.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted hard: sampling adequacy, concentration correction and imaging-functional discordance all matter to one treatment decision.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback explains why AVS is needed, but gives neither calculation nor the current side. The new table must be interpreted independently.
reasoning.repairRecord: Constructed original values and a left/right conflict instead of another question asking merely to order AVS.

definitions.name: Gavin Reed
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 60-year-old man, attends the clinic with confirmed primary aldosteronism and a right adrenal nodule. He has chosen surgery if a unilateral source can be shown. DST cortisol suppresses within range. The founder reviews the outside cosyntropin-stimulated AVS record.

nodes.objective: Identify failed adrenal vein selectivity before making a side-directed operation decision.

exhibit.caption: Constructed patient record; values are fictional observations.

nodes.stem: Which next localization plan should Gavin Reed receive before an adrenal operation?

choices.label: Repeat AVS at an experienced center
choices.rationale: The right-to-peripheral cortisol ratio is 1.1, so the right-labeled tube does not establish selective adrenal sampling.
choices.temptation: Checks the acquisition before interpreting laterality.
choices.counterfactual: If both veins were adequately selective and the corrected ratios lateralized, repeat sampling would not be needed.

choices.label: Use CT laterality for operative planning
choices.rationale: A failed functional sample does not convert an older patient's nodule into a proven secretory source.
choices.temptation: Uses a visible nodule to rescue an invalid invasive test.
choices.counterfactual: A narrowly selected very young-patient pathway may be considered separately; not this 60-year-old.

choices.label: Use these AVS ratios for operative planning
choices.rationale: A ratio based on an unselected right sample cannot support standard bilateral lateralization.
choices.temptation: Computes ratios before checking that both tubes came from the intended veins.
choices.counterfactual: Technically selective bilateral samples would permit standard ratio interpretation.

nodes.explanation: First establish what was sampled. Right cortisol is barely above peripheral cortisol, whereas left cortisol has a strong gradient. The right-labeled result is not a valid selective adrenal sample under stimulated conventions, so standard bilateral lateralization cannot be assigned from this record. Repeat expert AVS before side-directed surgery.

steps: Calculate right selectivity as 22/20 and recognize an inadequately selected sample.
Withhold side assignment and obtain a valid localization study instead of substituting CT or invalid ratios.
reasoning.closestError: Calculate a left/right ratio without validating the right sample.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Right-labeled cortisol 22 versus peripheral 20 after cosyntropin.
reasoning.counterfactual: With both selectivity ratios well above five and clear unilateral corrected secretion, the completed AVS could guide surgery without repetition.
reasoning.deletionTest: Cosyntropin, all cortisol values and the operative goal determine validity and next action. The right nodule creates the CT-rescue error; the aldosterone cells show why raw values cannot repair wrong-site sampling.
reasoning.cueAttack: No sample is called 'failed' or 'nonselective' before answering. The task does not name a missing repeat. Three localization policies refer to specific existing tests.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Localization policy before surgery after a questionable acquisition.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted hard because an apparently completed AVS can be less definitive than its header implies.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Standalone; no prior calculation or interpretation is supplied.
reasoning.repairRecord: New acquisition-validity objective; no unsupported unilateral-sampling rescue cutoff is taught.

definitions.name: Helen Grant
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 58-year-old woman, attends the clinic with confirmed primary aldosteronism and a left adrenal nodule. Cortisol suppresses normally. An experienced center's complete cosyntropin AVS record has adrenal/peripheral cortisol ratios of 12 on each side; corrected aldosterone/cortisol ratios are right 3 and left 3. Renal function and current potassium permit mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist treatment with monitoring.

nodes.objective: Select targeted medical treatment when technically valid AVS does not identify unilateral secretion despite a nodule.
nodes.stem: Which aldosterone-directed treatment should Helen Grant receive on this record?

choices.label: Spironolactone with laboratory monitoring
choices.rationale: Adequate sampling with equal corrected ratios does not support a unilateral operation; targeted MRA treatment fits bilateral secretion.
choices.temptation: Uses function rather than the nodule to choose treatment.
choices.counterfactual: Clear valid unilateral lateralization in a patient choosing surgery would favor unilateral adrenalectomy.

choices.label: Left adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: The left nodule is not accompanied by left-dominant secretion.
choices.temptation: Equates the CT lesion with the functional source.
choices.counterfactual: Valid left-dominant secretion would support left adrenalectomy.

choices.label: Right adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: There is no right-dominant secretion either; equal ratios do not identify a right surgical target.
choices.temptation: Overcorrects against the CT nodule by choosing the opposite gland.
choices.counterfactual: Valid right-dominant secretion would support right adrenalectomy.

nodes.explanation: Sampling is adequate, but corrected secretion is not lateralized. A visible nodule does not supply the missing functional evidence for unilateral surgery. Use a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with potassium and renal-function monitoring.

steps: Interpret technical adequacy separately from the equal corrected secretion ratios.
Choose targeted medical treatment because no unilateral source is demonstrated.
reasoning.closestError: Resect the left nodule despite symmetric AVS.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Both veins are adequately selected and corrected secretion is equal.
reasoning.counterfactual: A left-to-right corrected ratio well above four would support a different surgical discussion.
reasoning.deletionTest: The paired selectivity and secretion observations prevent mistaking invalid sampling for bilateral disease. Normal cortisol validates correction; monitoring eligibility prevents a medication contraindication from creating ambiguity.
reasoning.cueAttack: The stem does not label the AVS bilateral. The drug name and two operations are specific treatment choices; no generic individualized-plan key.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: PA-specific treatment selection after completed localization.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate: anatomical anchoring and the distinction between adequate and lateralized are credible errors.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Standalone. Ratios are supplied as the report's measurements because treatment interpretation, not arithmetic, is the objective.
reasoning.repairRecord: Added the medical branch absent from the four live CT-plus-AVS siblings.

definitions.name: Iris Cole
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 62-year-old woman, attends the clinic after lung-cancer treatment. Staging shows an isolated 2.8-cm adrenal lesion measuring 28 HU on unenhanced CT with FDG uptake. Oncology documents that tissue would change treatment. Cortisol assessment is normal. An outside plasma normetanephrine value is just above the printed reference interval; the sample was collected seated during a painful visit and interpreted using a supine reference interval.

nodes.objective: Review acquisition validity of a mild metanephrine elevation before clearing an adrenal biopsy.
nodes.stem: Which investigation should Iris Cole receive next in this adrenal evaluation?

choices.label: Repeat plasma metanephrines under supine conditions
choices.rationale: The mild abnormal result has a collection/reference mismatch and needs reassessment before invasive sampling.
choices.temptation: Checks validity without dismissing either secretory disease or the oncologic need for tissue.
choices.counterfactual: Repeated clearly elevated measurements under appropriate conditions would shift from repeat-screen validity to a functional-tumor pathway.

choices.label: Repeat adrenal CT with washout acquisition
choices.rationale: Another anatomical study does not resolve this biochemical collection problem or establish biopsy safety.
choices.temptation: Tries to resolve a functional uncertainty with better adrenal imaging.
choices.counterfactual: An incompletely characterized adrenal lesion without the present biochemical issue could require additional anatomical characterization.

choices.label: Repeat whole-body FDG-PET/CT
choices.rationale: PET uptake does not settle catecholamine secretion, and a staging study is already available.
choices.temptation: Treats a cancer staging modality as a functional exclusion test.
choices.counterfactual: A later oncologic restaging question could warrant repeat PET for a different objective.

nodes.explanation: Interpret the result in light of how it was obtained. A marginal result from a painful seated draw compared with a supine interval needs repeat standardized sampling. FDG uptake and a cancer history do not settle the endocrine safety question.

steps: Recognize a plausible false-positive collection/reference mismatch rather than treating the mild elevation as definitive.
Repeat the appropriate biochemical assessment before an adrenal needle procedure instead of using imaging to clear secretion.
reasoning.closestError: Accept FDG uptake as enough evidence of metastasis to bypass endocrine uncertainty.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Mild normetanephrine elevation obtained seated under stress but assessed against a supine interval.
reasoning.counterfactual: Repeated marked elevations under appropriate collection would make repeated screening less useful than endocrine tumor assessment and procedure deferral.
reasoning.deletionTest: Unenhanced indeterminate morphology, management-changing histology and existing PET establish why biopsy is considered. The sampling posture, stress and interval determine why this assay should be repeated.
reasoning.cueAttack: The report gives actual collection conditions, not a sentence announcing that they were inadequate. All options are repeat investigations, so the key is not the sole cautious information-gathering plan.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Next investigation addressing an unresolved adrenal evaluation.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted hard: the resident must separate malignancy probability, secretion and test validity.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node. Feedback does not give the next node's actual hormone result or definitive operation order.
reasoning.repairRecord: New meaning replaces a rote biopsy-safety association with acquisition review; no old prebiopsy FSRS history is reassigned.

nodes.objective: Use reliable positive metanephrine findings to defer a planned cancer-staging adrenal biopsy.
nodes.currentUpdate: Repeat testing was collected under the laboratory's supine protocol. Plasma metanephrine is 4.8 times its upper reference limit and normetanephrine is 5.2 times its upper reference limit. The needle-biopsy request remains pending; the adrenal lesion is the only potential distant site.
nodes.stem: How should Iris Cole's adrenal biopsy request be handled on these repeat findings?

choices.label: Defer biopsy for endocrine tumor assessment
choices.rationale: The repeat findings are no longer explained by the earlier collection mismatch; hormone activity must be assessed before the needle procedure.
choices.temptation: Reinterprets the reliable new evidence despite the cancer-staging incentive.
choices.counterfactual: A reliable normal functional assessment with the other biopsy criteria fulfilled could permit biopsy consideration.

choices.label: Proceed with CT-guided adrenal core biopsy
choices.rationale: A management-changing tissue indication does not override the endocrine safety boundary.
choices.temptation: Prioritizes tissue staging over reliable functional evidence.
choices.counterfactual: Reliable exclusion of hormone excess with indeterminate imaging and a management-changing result would restore biopsy consideration.

choices.label: Proceed with ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration
choices.rationale: Changing needle size or imaging guidance does not remove the hazard of manipulating a catecholamine-producing lesion.
choices.temptation: Treats a less invasive needle technique as a workaround.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriate nonadrenal sampling target with no such endocrine concern can have a different tissue pathway.

nodes.explanation: The repeated appropriately collected results require endocrine evaluation before any adrenal needle procedure. Management-changing tissue, an isolated lesion and FDG uptake do not remove that boundary. Changing biopsy technique does not solve the functional concern. This does not select an adrenal drug regimen or prove a universal numeric diagnostic cutoff.

steps: Reassess the repeated results as reliable marked abnormalities rather than the prior marginal collection artifact.
Apply the functional safety boundary to the proposed needle procedure despite the incentive for cancer staging.
reasoning.closestError: Proceed with a smaller needle because tissue could change cancer treatment.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Both appropriately collected repeat metabolites are several-fold above their own laboratory upper limits.
reasoning.counterfactual: If reliable repeat biochemical evaluation excluded hormone excess, the remaining management-changing indeterminate lesion could be considered for biopsy.
reasoning.deletionTest: The new acquisition and values are indispensable: deleting the update leaves the earlier validity uncertainty unresolved. The isolated lesion retains the oncologic pressure to obtain tissue.
reasoning.cueAttack: Replaced a generic procedure-planning key versus resection with three decisions about the actual biopsy request. The key's safety rationale is after the answer; no pre-answer sentence calls the lesion a pheochromocytoma.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: Disposition of the adrenal needle-biopsy request.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: a changed reliable assay must outweigh PET-based metastatic attribution and the small-needle workaround.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Earlier feedback asks for valid reassessment, not cancellation of all biopsies. The current reliable abnormal results earn the procedural decision.
reasoning.repairRecord: Reused the N3 functional-evidence concept and made the new data consequential. Prior N3 exact versions remain retained.

definitions.name: Leah Rowan
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 40-year-old woman, attends the endocrine-surgery clinic with medullary thyroid carcinoma and a germline RET pathogenic variant. Her father had an adrenal tumor. She also reports recurrent kidney stones. She has no episodic palpitations. Thyroid surgery is planned after staging.

nodes.objective: Apply the hereditary endocrine pattern to a specific preoperative biochemical assessment rather than reciting a syndrome name.
nodes.stem: Which additional endocrine testing plan should Leah Rowan receive before thyroid surgery?

choices.label: Metanephrines with calcium and PTH
choices.rationale: The hereditary thyroid context requires a pheochromocytoma screen even without spells; stones make the parathyroid axis relevant.
choices.temptation: Uses syndrome implications to select the two relevant endocrine axes.
choices.counterfactual: A different supported syndrome phenotype could warrant another biochemical pattern.

choices.label: Cortisol screening with calcium and PTH
choices.rationale: It addresses the stone/parathyroid axis but substitutes cortisol for the relevant adrenal medullary screen.
choices.temptation: Treats all hereditary adrenal concerns as cortical hormone excess.
choices.counterfactual: An adrenal cortical lesion with a separate parathyroid issue could require cortisol-focused workup.

choices.label: Metanephrines with prolactin and IGF-1
choices.rationale: It retains the relevant adrenal screen but substitutes a pituitary axis for the represented parathyroid concern.
choices.temptation: Blends MEN1-style pituitary associations into the RET-linked pattern.
choices.counterfactual: A separate pituitary phenotype with catecholamine symptoms could justify those axes.

choices.label: Cortisol screening with prolactin and IGF-1
choices.rationale: Neither component addresses the principal additional MEN2 axes represented here.
choices.temptation: Uses generic endocrine tumor testing instead of this hereditary pattern.
choices.counterfactual: A cortical/pituitary clinical problem could require these tests for a different objective.

nodes.explanation: The RET-associated thyroid history directs attention to adrenal medullary and parathyroid disease. Obtain metanephrines despite absent classic spells, and assess calcium/PTH in this stone-forming patient. The task asks for cross-organ preparation, not a syndrome-label recital or thyroid operation extent.

steps: Link the hereditary medullary thyroid and family adrenal history to the appropriate additional endocrine axes.
Apply that pattern to perioperative biochemical testing despite absent catecholamine spells.
reasoning.closestError: Choose a general cortisol/pituitary panel or omit adrenal testing because palpitations are absent.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with germline RET, family adrenal history and recurrent stones.
reasoning.counterfactual: A documented MEN1 pituitary/pancreatic phenotype rather than RET-linked medullary cancer would change the appropriate syndrome-directed workup.
reasoning.deletionTest: Histology and genotype fix the syndrome; family history and stones establish the two axes; the symptom negative tests whether asymptomatic status wrongly overrides screening. No genotype-specific age threshold is invented.
reasoning.cueAttack: Four options balance the two adrenal and two companion components; each appears twice. No majority-component or novelty pattern uniquely assembles the key. All testing bundles have timing metadata.
reasoning.stageAndCategory: One preoperative endocrine testing plan, with balanced paired laboratory components.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate: clinically applied syndrome consequences are harder than the approved triad-name siblings, but the paired structure needs independent cue review.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node. Feedback names tests only and does not state the later operative sequence.
reasoning.repairRecord: New meaning under a new concept identity; exact approved recognition questions and their histories remain untouched.

nodes.objective: Prioritize a functioning adrenal lesion over nonemergent thyroid and parathyroid operations in a MEN2 context.
nodes.currentUpdate: Leah's staging shows regional cervical nodes with medullary carcinoma but no distant metastases. She has a patent airway without stridor. Plasma metanephrine and normetanephrine are repeatedly several-fold above their laboratory upper limits, and CT identifies a right adrenal mass. Calcium is mildly above its interval with unsuppressed PTH; she has no acute hypercalcemic illness.
nodes.stem: After the appropriate shared perioperative preparation, which operation should Leah Rowan undergo first?

choices.label: Right adrenalectomy
choices.rationale: Functioning pheochromocytoma takes priority before thyroid intervention in this nonemergency MEN2 setting.
choices.temptation: Weighs biochemical adrenal activity against node-positive thyroid disease and chronic parathyroid disease.
choices.counterfactual: With reliable exclusion of a functioning adrenal tumor, the thyroid operation can regain priority.

choices.label: Thyroidectomy with indicated neck dissection
choices.rationale: Regional thyroid spread is important but does not outweigh the represented functioning adrenal perioperative risk without an airway emergency.
choices.temptation: Prioritizes the malignant lesion automatically over a functional endocrine hazard.
choices.counterfactual: A reliable negative adrenal assessment would change the sequence; a true airway emergency would require a different individualized emergency pathway.

choices.label: Parathyroid exploration with indicated resection
choices.rationale: Chronic mild PTH-dependent hypercalcemia is not the immediate operative priority in this record.
choices.temptation: Treats recurrent stones and biochemical hyperparathyroidism before the functional adrenal concern.
choices.counterfactual: After adrenal control, a separate organ-specific parathyroid indication can be addressed in the appropriate sequence.

nodes.explanation: The adrenal measurements change the order of the represented elective operations. Prepare and address the catecholamine-producing adrenal lesion before thyroid intervention.
